MARA Holdings (MARA) Mined More Bitcoin, but Revenue Fell 27%
Mon, October 19, 2026 at 2:41 PM CDT 4 min read
MARA Holdings (NASDAQ:MARA) mined 2,422 bitcoin in the second quarter, a little more than it mined a year earlier. Yet revenue fell 27% to $174.9 million because the average price of each coin it produced was far lower.
That gap explains why the company wants to stop being known as a bitcoin miner. It now describes itself as an owner of power-ready land and electricity, and it hopes to rent that capacity to AI companies. But mining still pays the bills and no AI customer has signed on yet, so the question is whether a customer arrives before the bitcoin cushion thins.
MARA runs 19 data centers, most filled with machines that earn bitcoin by processing transactions, and it holds a large stash of the coin. It wants to turn some sites into data centers that rent computing space to AI customers. On the evidence so far, it is a bitcoin miner paying for an AI transition that has no customer yet. Investors who want more stocks like this can find MARA in our recent list, 9 Best Bitcoin Stocks to Buy Now.
MARA Holdings (MARA) Mined More Bitcoin, but Revenue Fell 27%
The company's reported results still move with bitcoin's price. MARA posted a net loss of $611.3 million in the second quarter, and $343.0 million of that came from marking its bitcoin down to market value. It is a paper loss, but it landed on the line investors read as profit. Mining itself kept growing, with more machines running than a year earlier even as each coin was worth less.
Sales grew about 190.9% a year over the past five years, a long record of growth. But over the past 12 months MARA lost $3.46 billion on $804.22 million in sales, so the growth never reached profit. If you own the shares, you own a bet on bitcoin's price and a bet on AI demand at the same time.
Management's answer is power. MARA is waiting on regulatory approval for Long Ridge, a power plant with more than 70% of its output sold under long-term contracts. Management expects it to add earnings once it closes. MARA also secured rights to a powered land site in Matagorda County, Texas, and together the two would lift its power portfolio to as much as 4.8 gigawatts.
No customer has signed yet. Management told shareholders it is confident of signing at least one lease before year-end, working with its partner Starwood. For investors looking to add AI power exposure, our list of 10 Best AI Energy Stocks to Buy in 2026 covers more names.
The company took on $600.0 million of new bitcoin-backed loans to help fund Long Ridge, and it bought no bitcoin in the quarter while its holdings fell 29% to 35,577 coins. If no tenant signs, the company will have borrowed against the asset that protects it.
The plan survives this, because the power assets are lined up and the lease timeline is management's own. It does limit how much credit the company deserves until a contract exists.
Because MARA loses money, the usual earnings test does not apply. The forward P/E, which divides a stock's price by expected earnings, shows no meaningful value for the company, so the stock is not priced on earnings at all. Companies in its sector carry a median forward P/E of 21.01, which shows what investors pay for expected earnings, and MARA has none to compare.
Among hedge funds, holders of MARA numbered 27 in the second quarter of 2026, up from 25 in the first quarter. The count comes from quarterly filings, so it shows professional interest edging up even though the company still loses money. If you're looking for lower-priced stocks that hedge funds hold, check out 10 Best US Stocks to Buy Under $20: Ranked by Hedge Funds.
On the other side, short interest stands at 29.84% of shares outstanding, which means traders have borrowed and sold a large share of the stock, betting the price will fall. A reading that high shows many traders doubt the story will deliver.
So the puzzle at the start has a plain answer. MARA mined more bitcoin and still reported less revenue because its results follow bitcoin's price, and the AI plan has not changed that yet. The stock is priced on that plan, which makes the lease management expects before year-end the thing to watch.
While we acknowledge the risk and potential of MARA as an investment, our conviction lies in the belief that some AI stocks hold greater promise for delivering higher returns and doing so within a shorter time frame. Cryptocurrency mining stocks are brushing off a fresh round of analyst price target cuts, and buyers are stepping back in after a sharp selloff. MARA Holdings (NASDAQ:MARA | MARA Price Prediction) stock is rising 4% to $7.65 this afternoon. Similarly, Hut 8 (NASDAQ:HUT) shares are up 4% to $70.61, keeping pace with MARA stock.
Riot Platforms (NASDAQ:RIOT) stock is lagging both peers, up by only 0.5% to $14.04. Piper Sandler cut its price targets on MARA, Riot and Hut 8 shares in the same note, so the gains in MARA and Hut 8 shares show buyers treating the cuts as largely priced in.
Bitcoin (CRYPTO:BTC) is up 0.7% to $82,519 over a 24-hour window, well behind the rally in MARA or Hut 8 shares. That gap suggests MARA and Hut 8 shares are rallying more on their own rebound than on any lift from the cryptocurrency.
Piper Sandler Trims Targets on Rate and Credit Worries
In a new note, Piper Sandler analyst Patrick Moley cut price targets on MARA, Riot and Hut 8 shares, citing hotter inflation and higher oil prices that revived rate-hike concerns. Moley also pointed to credit markets repricing the debt that funds data center buildouts, along with uncertainty over planned AI capital spending. Each of those factors points straight at the financing behind data center plans at MARA, Riot and Hut 8.
Piper Sandler still maintained that MARA, Riot and Hut 8 shares look attractive after their recent selloff, and the firm kept an Overweight rating on MARA stock. Trading in MARA, Riot and Hut 8 shares initially turned lower after the note before reversing higher.
Cantor Fitzgerald had already cut its price targets on Riot and Hut 8 shares on October 16, so Piper Sandler’s note adds to a string of recent reductions for both names. Hut 8 stock is rallying through both rounds of cuts, while Riot stock is barely moving.
Power Sites Tie Miners to Bitcoin and Borrowing Costs
MARA, Riot and Hut 8 began as Bitcoin miners and are adding AI and high-performance computing data center businesses at existing power sites. That shift ties MARA, Riot and Hut 8 shares to both the Bitcoin price and the cost of financing data center construction, which is also why the power, cooling, and networking suppliers behind the expansion keep showing up in our free AI infrastructure report. Higher rates and repriced credit can lift the cost of each new build, which is why Moley’s concerns land directly on this corner of the market.
The CoinShares Bitcoin Mining and Digital Power ETF (NASDAQ:WGMI) is up 1% to $31.95. For broad-market context, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA:SPY) is up 0.3% to $768.63, a much smaller move than the mining fund. Both funds trail MARA and Hut 8 shares, while Riot shares sit below the mining ETF’s gain.
Data Center Debt Is the Next Hurdle for MARA
Another hurdle for MARA is whether credit markets keep repricing data center debt. Hotter inflation, higher oil prices and renewed rate-hike concerns all feed into that financing cost. Traders can watch for whether Riot stock joins the rebound in MARA and Hut 8 stock.
Piper Sandler’s Overweight rating on MARA stock and its view that MARA, Riot and Hut 8 shares look attractive after the selloff give buyers a reason for confidence. Piper Sandler’s lower price targets still argue for patience. Investors should consider keeping their position sizes modest until the data center financing picture resolves.

The largest Bitcoin miner just moved 1,000 BTC onto exchanges while its holdings have quietly shrunk by thousands of coins, and now Michael Saylor is hinting at a buy. Whether that signals a sale, a loan, or something else changes…

MARA Holdings (NASDAQ:MARA | MARA Price Prediction), the largest publicly traded Bitcoin miner, transferred 1,000 Bitcoin (CRYPTO:BTC), valued at around $82.8 million, to the Binance and Gate exchanges over five days, according to the on-chain tracker Lookonchain. MARA hasn’t explained these transfers. So, is MARA selling Bitcoin?
In contrast, Michael Saylor, executive chairman of Strategy Inc. (NASDAQ:MSTR), signaled more Bitcoin purchases. He tweeted, “We found room for more orange,” his usual hint at another purchase. Strategy Inc. holds 848,250 BTC and last reported buying 250 BTC, though it has not made a new announcement yet.
Bitcoin trades at approximately $82,720. MARA shares were at $7.70 premarket, up 2.3% from the previous close of $7.53, even though they remain down 20.2% for the week and 30.3% for the month.
Meanwhile, Strategy Inc. was trading at around $140 premarket, down 9.6% for the week, as investors worry that a stock index could drop the company.
MARA’s Mining Revenue Falls as Its Costs Climb
MARA primarily earns revenue through Bitcoin mining, where specialized computers compete to add new blocks to the network and earn newly mined coins. Its revenue decreased to $174.9 million in the second quarter, down from $238.5 million the previous year. A 28% drop in Bitcoin’s average price cut revenue by $65.9 million.
MARA’s hashrate, the total computing power its machines contribute to the network, rose to 70.3 exahashes per second. However, the cost of energy needed to mine each Bitcoin has increased to $38,690 from $33,735 a year ago. Management attributed this rise to increased mining difficulty, which occurs when more machines come online.
About $343 million of MARA’s $611.3 million net loss came from a mark-to-market loss, which is a paper loss from valuing its Bitcoin at lower prices without selling any coins. Management noted that every $10,000 change in Bitcoin’s price affects that line by approximately $350 million. MARA ended the quarter with $421.3 million in cash.
MARA Is Spending Heavily on Power and AI
MARA is also moving into energy and is acquiring Long Ridge Energy, a gas-fired power plant, in a $1.5 billion deal, including debt. MARA plans to assume about $900 million of Long Ridge’s debt, and the deal is pending approval from the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC).
MARA has also secured rights to a 2 GW-powered site in Matagorda County, Texas, with plans to convert most of its capacity for AI and high-performance computing through a joint venture with Starwood. Its Exaion unit already operates an AI cloud in Europe, ensuring customer data complies with European regulations. We also cover seven suppliers benefiting from similar shifts in a free AI infrastructure report.
To finance these ventures, MARA borrowed $600 million using Bitcoin-backed credit facilities with Coinbase (NASDAQ:COIN) and Two Prime at an average interest rate of 7.6%. Lenders can claim the pledged Bitcoin if MARA fails to repay, and the new loans left 54% of MARA’s Bitcoin pledged as collateral.
Management has indicated that MARA will continue to sell Bitcoin selectively to fund operations. Its filings support this, showing MARA held 35,577 BTC at the end of June, down from 49,951 BTC a year earlier, with no updated figures released since its August 6 earnings call.
Saylor’s Buy Hint Cannot Offset MARA’s Exchange Deposits
Companies that send coins to an exchange are often preparing to sell, as exchanges facilitate trades between buyers and sellers. However, companies also move coins for other reasons, like lending them out, using them as collateral, or hedging against price fluctuations. MARA does engage in lending; in the second quarter, it had 4,742 BTC out on loan, generating about $4.3 million in interest.
While the deposits may imply a sale, they don’t prove one. MARA reported Coinbase and Two Prime as lenders for the new credit lines, yet the coins were sent to Binance and Gate. MARA has not disclosed any specific buyers, sale prices, or proceeds, and it hasn’t confirmed the wallet labels Lookonchain assigned.
Saylor’s tweet also warrants close examination. As the head of the largest corporate holder of Bitcoin, he promotes the asset central to his company’s balance sheet, but his post mentions no specific amounts, dates, or funding sources. Strategy Inc. has also sold Bitcoin this year, with $218.4 million sold to date under its Bitcoin monetization program as of its second-quarter report.
During the same period as Strategy Inc.’s last 250 BTC purchase, the company also spent $192.4 million buying back preferred shares instead of buying more Bitcoin. MARA’s deposit of 1,000 BTC is four times that 250 BTC buy.
Is MARA Selling Bitcoin? What Does It Mean for Prices?
Signs suggest MARA may be selling, or preparing to sell, some of its Bitcoin. The coins went to trading platforms, and MARA has said it sells Bitcoin selectively. It also has a power plant deal, AI expansion plans, and rising mining costs to fund. Selling Bitcoin can generate cash without diluting shareholders, but it may weigh slightly on Bitcoin prices since the proceeds go into infrastructure.
MARA’s next update should settle it. If the report shows fewer than 35,577 BTC and mentions any sales, the coins were sold; steady holdings, with more coins lent or pledged, would suggest a collateral move. An 8-K filing showing Strategy Inc. buying more than 1,000 BTC would mean one buyer absorbed the miner’s coins. MARA’s shares could still rise on FERC approval or new leases, even if Bitcoin prices stall.

MARA Has Lost 64% in a Year: Piper Sandler Sees 53% Upside ©WiR_Pixs from pixabay, Karola G from Pexels via Canva
MARA Holdings has lost 64% of its value in a year, and Piper Sandler cut its target to $11 from $13 today while keeping its Overweight rating.
The $11 target is roughly 53% above this morning's price and sits near the bottom of a Street range that runs from $10 to $30.
A lower bitcoin price led to a $611.3 million second-quarter loss, and investors are still waiting for the AI data center lease management expects by year-end.
The numbers support Piper's call, but it depends on bitcoin and on MARA signing its first lease.
MARA Holdings (MARA:NASDAQ) has lost 64% of its value over the past year (through Monday's close), and Piper Sandler just cut its price target for the third time in 2026. Even so, the firm's new $11 target sits 53% above this morning's price.
MARA's second quarter shows the problem well. Revenue fell 27% from $227.2 million a year earlier to $174.9 million as bitcoin's average price dropped 28%, and the company lost $611.3 million, about $343 million of it from marking bitcoin to market.
Management's answer is the AI pivot. On the Aug. 6 call, CEO Fred Thiel said MARA remains "confident in our ability to sign at least 2 leases before year-end."
No lease has been announced yet, and the clock on that year-end promise is running. Then October got rough for the whole group, as hotter inflation data and worries about debt-funded AI build-outs hit the miners. MARA went from $11.33 at the end of September to $7.38 at Monday's close.
Piper still says buy, just at a lower price
Piper Sandler analyst Patrick Moley stuck with his Overweight rating today but lowered his target to $11 from $13, his third cut this year after trimming it to $16 in January and to $13 in July.
Does $11 add up?
The rest of the Street has been lowering its sights too. The analysts' average target has slipped from $23.32 a year ago to $18.61 now, while the stock fell much further…
MARA (MARA): analysts' consensus (mean) price target, $ per share, last year (TIKR)
That leaves Piper's $11 near the bottom of a range that runs from $10 to $30. Nine analysts rate the stock Buy or Outperform, against one Underperform and one Sell. And $11 is roughly where MARA traded three weeks ago: it closed at $11.33 on Sept. 30.
Revenue estimates are less friendly. Analysts expect $707 million this year, down from $907 million in 2025, then $805 million in 2027 and just $606 million in 2028…
MARA (MARA): revenue, actual and consensus estimates, $ millions, fiscal 2024–2028 (TIKR)
A signed lease is the most likely thing to lift those numbers.
On TIKR's normalized estimates, MARA trades at just over 4x forward earnings, and Piper's target implies 6.3x. The few analysts who publish GAAP forecasts still expect losses in 2026 and 2027, though smaller ones than a month ago.
A modest target, with a bitcoin-sized risk
The risk is the balance sheet. After $600 million of new bitcoin-backed borrowing, 54% of MARA's bitcoin is pledged as collateral. MARA also expects to take on about $900 million of debt when its $1.5 billion Long Ridge acquisition closes.
My take: the numbers support Piper's call. It only asks for a return to September's price at a single-digit multiple, while loss estimates are shrinking.
The test is the leases. If the first one lands before Dec. 31, along with FERC's approval of the Long Ridge deal, $11 starts to look conservative. If the year ends without one, expect more target cuts.

MARA Holdings (MARA) Mined More Bitcoin, but Revenue Fell 27%
Mon, October 19, 2026 at 2:41 PM CDT 4 min read
MARA Holdings (NASDAQ:MARA) mined 2,422 bitcoin in the second quarter, a little more than it mined a year earlier. Yet revenue fell 27% to $174.9 million because the average price of each coin it produced was far lower.
That gap explains why the company wants to stop being known as a bitcoin miner. It now describes itself as an owner of power-ready land and electricity, and it hopes to rent that capacity to AI companies. But mining still pays the bills and no AI customer has signed on yet, so the question is whether a customer arrives before the bitcoin cushion thins.
MARA runs 19 data centers, most filled with machines that earn bitcoin by processing transactions, and it holds a large stash of the coin. It wants to turn some sites into data centers that rent computing space to AI customers. On the evidence so far, it is a bitcoin miner paying for an AI transition that has no customer yet. Investors who want more stocks like this can find MARA in our recent list, 9 Best Bitcoin Stocks to Buy Now.
MARA Holdings (MARA) Mined More Bitcoin, but Revenue Fell 27%
The company's reported results still move with bitcoin's price. MARA posted a net loss of $611.3 million in the second quarter, and $343.0 million of that came from marking its bitcoin down to market value. It is a paper loss, but it landed on the line investors read as profit. Mining itself kept growing, with more machines running than a year earlier even as each coin was worth less.
Sales grew about 190.9% a year over the past five years, a long record of growth. But over the past 12 months MARA lost $3.46 billion on $804.22 million in sales, so the growth never reached profit. If you own the shares, you own a bet on bitcoin's price and a bet on AI demand at the same time.
Management's answer is power. MARA is waiting on regulatory approval for Long Ridge, a power plant with more than 70% of its output sold under long-term contracts. Management expects it to add earnings once it closes. MARA also secured rights to a powered land site in Matagorda County, Texas, and together the two would lift its power portfolio to as much as 4.8 gigawatts.
No customer has signed yet. Management told shareholders it is confident of signing at least one lease before year-end, working with its partner Starwood. For investors looking to add AI power exposure, our list of 10 Best AI Energy Stocks to Buy in 2026 covers more names.
The company took on $600.0 million of new bitcoin-backed loans to help fund Long Ridge, and it bought no bitcoin in the quarter while its holdings fell 29% to 35,577 coins. If no tenant signs, the company will have borrowed against the asset that protects it.
The plan survives this, because the power assets are lined up and the lease timeline is management's own. It does limit how much credit the company deserves until a contract exists.
Because MARA loses money, the usual earnings test does not apply. The forward P/E, which divides a stock's price by expected earnings, shows no meaningful value for the company, so the stock is not priced on earnings at all. Companies in its sector carry a median forward P/E of 21.01, which shows what investors pay for expected earnings, and MARA has none to compare.
Among hedge funds, holders of MARA numbered 27 in the second quarter of 2026, up from 25 in the first quarter. The count comes from quarterly filings, so it shows professional interest edging up even though the company still loses money. If you're looking for lower-priced stocks that hedge funds hold, check out 10 Best US Stocks to Buy Under $20: Ranked by Hedge Funds.
On the other side, short interest stands at 29.84% of shares outstanding, which means traders have borrowed and sold a large share of the stock, betting the price will fall. A reading that high shows many traders doubt the story will deliver.
So the puzzle at the start has a plain answer. MARA mined more bitcoin and still reported less revenue because its results follow bitcoin's price, and the AI plan has not changed that yet. The stock is priced on that plan, which makes the lease management expects before year-end the thing to watch.
While we acknowledge the risk and potential of MARA as an investment, our conviction lies in the belief that some AI stocks hold greater promise for delivering higher returns and doing so within a shorter time frame. If you are looking for an AI stock that is more promising than MARA and that has 10,000% upside potential, check out our report about this cheapest AI stock.

Cryptocurrency Stocks Rise Despite Piper Sandler Price Target Cuts: MARA and Hut 8 Gain 4%, Riot Holds Flat
Piper Sandler just slashed price targets on three major crypto mining stocks, yet buyers rushed back in anyway. Whether that confidence survives the next wave of data center financing concerns is the real question hanging over MARA, Hut 8, and…
Published October 20, 2026, 1:05pm ET · 3 min read
Market Movers desk. Editor: David Moadel.
This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.
Cryptocurrency mining stocks are brushing off a fresh round of analyst price target cuts, and buyers are stepping back in after a sharp selloff. MARA Holdings (NASDAQ:MARA | MARA Price Prediction) stock is rising 4% to $7.65 this afternoon. Similarly, Hut 8 (NASDAQ:HUT) shares are up 4% to $70.61, keeping pace with MARA stock.
Riot Platforms (NASDAQ:RIOT) stock is lagging both peers, up by only 0.5% to $14.04. Piper Sandler cut its price targets on MARA, Riot and Hut 8 shares in the same note, so the gains in MARA and Hut 8 shares show buyers treating the cuts as largely priced in.
Bitcoin (CRYPTO:BTC) is up 0.7% to $82,519 over a 24-hour window, well behind the rally in MARA or Hut 8 shares. That gap suggests MARA and Hut 8 shares are rallying more on their own rebound than on any lift from the cryptocurrency.
Piper Sandler Trims Targets on Rate and Credit Worries
In a new note, Piper Sandler analyst Patrick Moley cut price targets on MARA, Riot and Hut 8 shares, citing hotter inflation and higher oil prices that revived rate-hike concerns. Moley also pointed to credit markets repricing the debt that funds data center buildouts, along with uncertainty over planned AI capital spending. Each of those factors points straight at the financing behind data center plans at MARA, Riot and Hut 8.
Piper Sandler still maintained that MARA, Riot and Hut 8 shares look attractive after their recent selloff, and the firm kept an Overweight rating on MARA stock. Trading in MARA, Riot and Hut 8 shares initially turned lower after the note before reversing higher.
Cantor Fitzgerald had already cut its price targets on Riot and Hut 8 shares on October 16, so Piper Sandler’s note adds to a string of recent reductions for both names. Hut 8 stock is rallying through both rounds of cuts, while Riot stock is barely moving.
Power Sites Tie Miners to Bitcoin and Borrowing Costs
MARA, Riot and Hut 8 began as Bitcoin miners and are adding AI and high-performance computing data center businesses at existing power sites. That shift ties MARA, Riot and Hut 8 shares to both the Bitcoin price and the cost of financing data center construction, which is also why the power, cooling, and networking suppliers behind the expansion keep showing up in our free AI infrastructure report. Higher rates and repriced credit can lift the cost of each new build, which is why Moley’s concerns land directly on this corner of the market.
The CoinShares Bitcoin Mining and Digital Power ETF (NASDAQ:WGMI) is up 1% to $31.95. For broad-market context, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA:SPY) is up 0.3% to $768.63, a much smaller move than the mining fund. Both funds trail MARA and Hut 8 shares, while Riot shares sit below the mining ETF’s gain.
Data Center Debt Is the Next Hurdle for MARA
Another hurdle for MARA is whether credit markets keep repricing data center debt. Hotter inflation, higher oil prices and renewed rate-hike concerns all feed into that financing cost. Traders can watch for whether Riot stock joins the rebound in MARA and Hut 8 stock.
Piper Sandler’s Overweight rating on MARA stock and its view that MARA, Riot and Hut 8 shares look attractive after the selloff give buyers a reason for confidence. Piper Sandler’s lower price targets still argue for patience. Investors should consider keeping their position sizes modest until the data center financing picture resolves.

MARA Holdings Sends $81M to Galaxy—What Next?
MARA Holdings sent 996 BTC worth $81.13 million to Galaxy Digital, raising questions about a sale as the US miner expands into AI.
By Maxwell MutumaOctober 9, 2026No Comments3 Mins Read
MARA Holdings transferred 996.105 BTC worth approximately $81.13 million to Galaxy Digital.
Blockchain records have not confirmed whether Galaxy Digital sold the transferred Bitcoin.
MARA sold 23,093 BTC for approximately $1.6 billion during the first half of 2026.
The company’s Bitcoin holdings stood at 35,577 BTC on June 30, down from 53,822 BTC at the end of 2025.
MARA is expanding into AI and high-performance computing while managing its Bitcoin treasury and debt obligations.
MARA Holdings transferred 996 Bitcoin, valued at $81.13 million, to a wallet linked to Galaxy Digital, according to blockchain tracker Lookonchain. The October 9 movement follows months of Bitcoin sales by the miner. However, available records do not establish whether Galaxy Digital sold the coins.
Transfer Raises Questions About Bitcoin Sale
Lookonchain identified the sending address as MARA Miner and the receiving address as Galaxy Digital. The transaction involved 996.105 BTC. Galaxy Digital offers trading and custody services, so a transfer to its wallets does not necessarily represent a sale.

Bitcoin recovered above $82,000 on Friday after declining during the week. Separately, US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds recorded $484.9 million in withdrawals on October 7. Those figures describe broader market conditions, not the purpose of MARA’s transaction.

AI Expansion Remains a Corporate Priority
MARA Holdings is increasing its focus on artificial intelligence and high-performance computing. Second-quarter revenue fell 27% to $174.9 million, while the company recorded a $611.3 million net loss.
The strategy comes amid expanding demand for AI data centers and computing infrastructure, with new construction and technical hiring accompanying industry investment. MARA has identified digital infrastructure as its primary growth focus.

Has MARA Ever Sold Its Bitcoin? The 1,000 BTC is a Fraction of Disclosed Holdings
MARA reported holding 35,577 BTC at the end of June, including 9,270 BTC that had been loaned out or pledged as collateral. Against that reported total, the latest 1,000 BTC represents roughly 2.8% of holdings, a meaningful flow to monitor but not a measure of realized selling pressure.
The company had already demonstrated that it will sell Bitcoin when it sees a reason to do so. MARA was selling 2,213 Bitcoin during the second quarter at an average price of $73,078, and separately sold 15,133 BTC in March to fund convertible-debt buybacks.
MARA also said it expected to continue selling Bitcoin opportunistically. That policy makes a sale a plausible interpretation of the exchange deposits, but it does not establish that these particular coins were sold; the distinction is central to assessing the potential supply impact.

Bitcoin’s rebound from lower levels therefore did not remove the near-term question of whether additional miner supply would meet sufficient demand.
MARA’s third-quarter results are the next company reporting checkpoint for how many of the deposited coins, if any, were sold. Until those disclosures or other evidence establish a disposal, the accurate description is an exchange inflow that has stirred fresh Bitcoin selling speculation.

Bitcoin News: MARA Sent 1,000 BTC to Exchanges as Saylor Hints at Another Buy. Is the Biggest Miner Selling?
The largest Bitcoin miner just moved 1,000 BTC onto exchanges while its holdings have quietly shrunk by thousands of coins, and now Michael Saylor is hinting at a buy. Whether that signals a sale, a loan, or something else changes…
Published October 19, 2026, 5:51am ET · 4 min read
The Crypto Desk desk. Editor: Sam Daodu.
This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.
This conceptual image illustrates the intricate process of Bitcoin mining and its connection to the broader cryptocurrency network, reflecting the activities of companies like MARA. © thodonal88 / Shutterstock.com
MARA Holdings (NASDAQ:MARA | MARA Price Prediction), the largest publicly traded Bitcoin miner, transferred 1,000 Bitcoin (CRYPTO:BTC), valued at around $82.8 million, to the Binance and Gate exchanges over five days, according to the on-chain tracker Lookonchain. MARA hasn’t explained these transfers. So, is MARA selling Bitcoin?
In contrast, Michael Saylor, executive chairman of Strategy Inc. (NASDAQ:MSTR), signaled more Bitcoin purchases. He tweeted, “We found room for more orange,” his usual hint at another purchase. Strategy Inc. holds 848,250 BTC and last reported buying 250 BTC, though it has not made a new announcement yet.
Bitcoin trades at approximately $82,720. MARA shares were at $7.70 premarket, up 2.3% from the previous close of $7.53, even though they remain down 20.2% for the week and 30.3% for the month.
Meanwhile, Strategy Inc. was trading at around $140 premarket, down 9.6% for the week, as investors worry that a stock index could drop the company.
MARA’s Mining Revenue Falls as Its Costs Climb
MARA primarily earns revenue through Bitcoin mining, where specialized computers compete to add new blocks to the network and earn newly mined coins. Its revenue decreased to $174.9 million in the second quarter, down from $238.5 million the previous year. A 28% drop in Bitcoin’s average price cut revenue by $65.9 million.
MARA’s hashrate, the total computing power its machines contribute to the network, rose to 70.3 exahashes per second. However, the cost of energy needed to mine each Bitcoin has increased to $38,690 from $33,735 a year ago. Management attributed this rise to increased mining difficulty, which occurs when more machines come online.
About $343 million of MARA’s $611.3 million net loss came from a mark-to-market loss, which is a paper loss from valuing its Bitcoin at lower prices without selling any coins. Management noted that every $10,000 change in Bitcoin’s price affects that line by approximately $350 million. MARA ended the quarter with $421.3 million in cash.
MARA Is Spending Heavily on Power and AI
MARA is also moving into energy and is acquiring Long Ridge Energy, a gas-fired power plant, in a $1.5 billion deal, including debt. MARA plans to assume about $900 million of Long Ridge’s debt, and the deal is pending approval from the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC).
MARA has also secured rights to a 2 GW-powered site in Matagorda County, Texas, with plans to convert most of its capacity for AI and high-performance computing through a joint venture with Starwood. Its Exaion unit already operates an AI cloud in Europe, ensuring customer data complies with European regulations. We also cover seven suppliers benefiting from similar shifts in a free AI infrastructure report.
To finance these ventures, MARA borrowed $600 million using Bitcoin-backed credit facilities with Coinbase (NASDAQ:COIN) and Two Prime at an average interest rate of 7.6%. Lenders can claim the pledged Bitcoin if MARA fails to repay, and the new loans left 54% of MARA’s Bitcoin pledged as collateral.
Management has indicated that MARA will continue to sell Bitcoin selectively to fund operations. Its filings support this, showing MARA held 35,577 BTC at the end of June, down from 49,951 BTC a year earlier, with no updated figures released since its August 6 earnings call.
Saylor’s Buy Hint Cannot Offset MARA’s Exchange Deposits
Companies that send coins to an exchange are often preparing to sell, as exchanges facilitate trades between buyers and sellers. However, companies also move coins for other reasons, like lending them out, using them as collateral, or hedging against price fluctuations. MARA does engage in lending; in the second quarter, it had 4,742 BTC out on loan, generating about $4.3 million in interest.
While the deposits may imply a sale, they don’t prove one. MARA reported Coinbase and Two Prime as lenders for the new credit lines, yet the coins were sent to Binance and Gate. MARA has not disclosed any specific buyers, sale prices, or proceeds, and it hasn’t confirmed the wallet labels Lookonchain assigned.
Saylor’s tweet also warrants close examination. As the head of the largest corporate holder of Bitcoin, he promotes the asset central to his company’s balance sheet, but his post mentions no specific amounts, dates, or funding sources. Strategy Inc. has also sold Bitcoin this year, with $218.4 million sold to date under its Bitcoin monetization program as of its second-quarter report.
During the same period as Strategy Inc.’s last 250 BTC purchase, the company also spent $192.4 million buying back preferred shares instead of buying more Bitcoin. MARA’s deposit of 1,000 BTC is four times that 250 BTC buy.
Is MARA Selling Bitcoin? What Does It Mean for Prices?
Signs suggest MARA may be selling, or preparing to sell, some of its Bitcoin. The coins went to trading platforms, and MARA has said it sells Bitcoin selectively. It also has a power plant deal, AI expansion plans, and rising mining costs to fund. Selling Bitcoin can generate cash without diluting shareholders, but it may weigh slightly on Bitcoin prices since the proceeds go into infrastructure.
MARA’s next update should settle it. If the report shows fewer than 35,577 BTC and mentions any sales, the coins were sold; steady holdings, with more coins lent or pledged, would suggest a collateral move. An 8-K filing showing Strategy Inc. buying more than 1,000 BTC would mean one buyer absorbed the miner’s coins. MARA’s shares could still rise on FERC approval or new leases, even if Bitcoin prices stall.

MARA Has Lost 64% in a Year: Piper Sandler Sees 53% Upside
Tue, October 20, 2026 at 12:45 PM CDT 4 min read
MARA Has Lost 64% in a Year: Piper Sandler Sees 53% Upside ©WiR_Pixs from pixabay, Karola G from Pexels via Canva
MARA Holdings has lost 64% of its value in a year, and Piper Sandler cut its target to $11 from $13 today while keeping its Overweight rating.
The $11 target is roughly 53% above this morning's price and sits near the bottom of a Street range that runs from $10 to $30.
A lower bitcoin price led to a $611.3 million second-quarter loss, and investors are still waiting for the AI data center lease management expects by year-end.
The numbers support Piper's call, but it depends on bitcoin and on MARA signing its first lease.
MARA Holdings (MARA:NASDAQ) has lost 64% of its value over the past year (through Monday's close), and Piper Sandler just cut its price target for the third time in 2026. Even so, the firm's new $11 target sits 53% above this morning's price.
MARA's second quarter shows the problem well. Revenue fell 27% from $227.2 million a year earlier to $174.9 million as bitcoin's average price dropped 28%, and the company lost $611.3 million, about $343 million of it from marking bitcoin to market.
Management's answer is the AI pivot. On the Aug. 6 call, CEO Fred Thiel said MARA remains "confident in our ability to sign at least 2 leases before year-end."
No lease has been announced yet, and the clock on that year-end promise is running. Then October got rough for the whole group, as hotter inflation data and worries about debt-funded AI build-outs hit the miners. MARA went from $11.33 at the end of September to $7.38 at Monday's close.
Piper still says buy, just at a lower price
Piper Sandler analyst Patrick Moley stuck with his Overweight rating today but lowered his target to $11 from $13, his third cut this year after trimming it to $16 in January and to $13 in July.
Does $11 add up?
The rest of the Street has been lowering its sights too. The analysts' average target has slipped from $23.32 a year ago to $18.61 now, while the stock fell much further…
MARA (MARA): analysts' consensus (mean) price target, $ per share, last year (TIKR)
That leaves Piper's $11 near the bottom of a range that runs from $10 to $30. Nine analysts rate the stock Buy or Outperform, against one Underperform and one Sell. And $11 is roughly where MARA traded three weeks ago: it closed at $11.33 on Sept. 30.
Revenue estimates are less friendly. Analysts expect $707 million this year, down from $907 million in 2025, then $805 million in 2027 and just $606 million in 2028…
MARA (MARA): revenue, actual and consensus estimates, $ millions, fiscal 2024–2028 (TIKR)
A signed lease is the most likely thing to lift those numbers.
On TIKR's normalized estimates, MARA trades at just over 4x forward earnings, and Piper's target implies 6.3x. The few analysts who publish GAAP forecasts still expect losses in 2026 and 2027, though smaller ones than a month ago.
A modest target, with a bitcoin-sized risk
The risk is the balance sheet. After $600 million of new bitcoin-backed borrowing, 54% of MARA's bitcoin is pledged as collateral. MARA also expects to take on about $900 million of debt when its $1.5 billion Long Ridge acquisition closes.
My take: the numbers support Piper's call. It only asks for a return to September's price at a single-digit multiple, while loss estimates are shrinking.
The test is the leases. If the first one lands before Dec. 31, along with FERC's approval of the Long Ridge deal, $11 starts to look conservative. If the year ends without one, expect more target cuts.

Gaming names around Take-Two tell a calmer story, and the contrast is sharp. Roblox (NYSE:RBLX) stock is flat at $49.60, holding steady even as Take-Two shares fall. Wells Fargo Cuts Near-Term Numbers but Keeps Its Overweight Call
Wells Fargo reiterated an Overweight rating and a $300 price target on Take-Two stock in the prior session. Beneath that headline, Wells Fargo trimmed its near-term bookings and adjusted EBITDA (earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization) estimates on weaker unit assumptions for the basketball franchise. A softer bridge matters because Take-Two still reports another quarter before the release changes its results.
Take-Two’s next quarterly report lands in early November, on a date the company hasn’t confirmed, and that release is where the guidance Wells Fargo highlighted may surface. The open question is whether the pre-release catalogue holds firm enough to support the valuation until Grand Theft Auto VI ships.

Grand Theft Auto VI Is Weeks Away. Is Take-Two Interactive (TTWO) Still a Buy at a Discount?
A video game company sitting on the most anticipated release in years would seem to deserve a premium price tag. Yet Take-Two Interactive Software (NASDAQ:TTWO) trades at a lower multiple than it has averaged over the past five years, with Grand Theft Auto VI only weeks away.
Take-Two owns Rockstar Games, the studio behind Grand Theft Auto and Red Dead Redemption, along with 2K's NBA 2K series and Zynga's mobile titles like Toon Blast and Words With Friends. It earns money when people buy its games, and even more from what they keep spending afterward on virtual currency, add-ons, and in-game items. Even with that lucrative pipeline, the video game publisher doesn't secure a spot among the 10 Best Undervalued Stocks to Buy in October. That leaves investors with a puzzle. Is the market underrating the biggest launch in the company's history, or quietly pricing in softness elsewhere in the portfolio? The answer depends on what happens after the launch-day buzz fades.
Is Cameco (CCJ) a Buy Before the Westinghouse Spin-Off?
Take-Two's real edge isn't one game. It's a catalog players keep returning to. In the fiscal first quarter of 2027, which ended in June, recurrent consumer spending made up 84% of net bookings (sales measured before accounting deferrals). That's money from people who already own the games and keep paying to play them.
The company's list of top contributors reads like a roll call of long-running franchises: NBA 2K, Grand Theft Auto, Red Dead Redemption, and mobile staples such as Toon Blast, Match Factory!, and Empires & Puzzles. Many of these are years old and still among its biggest earners. Annual sports releases run on that same repeat-spending model, which a major rival sports-game publisher depends on as well.
The fiscal first quarter wasn't a blowout. Net bookings slipped 3% to $1.39 billion, though that still landed slightly above management's guidance range. GAAP net revenue edged up to $1.53 billion from $1.50 billion, while the company posted a GAAP net loss of $34.1 million, or $0.18 per share.
The outlook is where the story lives. Management reiterated its fiscal 2027 target of $8.0 billion to $8.2 billion in net bookings, with GTA VI scheduled to arrive in November on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. CEO Strauss Zelnick said the company expects to sustain this new level of scale and generate strong cash flows. Even with that historic growth trajectory on the horizon, the video game publisher remains noticeably absent from the 10 Best Growth Stocks to Buy Now According to Billionaires. Put that full-year target next to a $1.39 billion quarter, and it's obvious how much rides on the holiday months. CNBC reported that a recent preview of the game pointed to blockbuster demand.
What If Mobile Keeps Sliding?
The strongest objection sits in Take-Two's largest platform. Mobile net bookings fell to $739.5 million from $792.8 million, still accounting for 53% of the total. Console net revenue moved the other way, climbing to $640.5 million from $550.6 million.
That split matters. GTA VI launches on consoles, so a shrinking mobile business would leave Take-Two leaning harder on a single franchise. It's a pressure other mobile-heavy game makers have felt too. Recurrent spending dipped only 1%, so the engine underneath hasn't stalled. But mobile is the piece to watch once the launch excitement settles.
At a forward P/E of 31.05, as of October 12, investors are paying about $31 for every $1 of expected earnings. That's far below Take-Two's 5-year average P/E of 51.25, even as the company heads into the biggest product cycle in its history. It still looks pricey next to the sector P/E of 12.29. But few companies in that group are staring at a growth spike like this one. Analysts expect EPS growth of 49.70% in 2028, a pace that makes a sector-average multiple a poor fit.
There's an accounting wrinkle, too. GAAP guidance for fiscal 2027 calls for just $0.55 to $0.75 per share, so today's valuation rests on the earnings investors expect after GTA VI ships, not on this year's accounting profit. That's a bet on execution, and a big one.
Here's the tension, then. A stock that historically commanded more than 50 times earnings now sits near 31 right before its defining release. Either the market doubts the GTA VI surge will last, or it's leaving room for upside if players keep spending long after launch. That valuation gap highlights how much the market demands proven, long-tail monetization, the kind seen when Tencent Music (TME) turns streaming into a sprawling entertainment machine, rather than relying entirely on a single console release window. Hedge fund interest has risen, with 84 funds holding the stock in the most recent quarter, up from 77 in the prior one. Short interest sits at 4.45% of float, suggesting relatively limited bearish positioning.
The evidence points to a stock priced for a big launch, but not necessarily a lasting one. At roughly 31 times expected earnings, well under its own five-year norm, Take-Two looks reasonably valued if GTA VI keeps players spending for years, the way its predecessor did.
The setup suits patient investors comfortable with a hit-driven business and willing to sit through launch-quarter volatility. Would the picture change? Another delay, or mobile declines deep enough to swallow the console gains, would make even this discounted multiple harder to defend

Take-Two Interactive Slides 5% as Wells Fargo Trims Estimates Behind $300 Target; Roblox Holds Flat, GameStop Barely Budges
Wells Fargo kept its bullish rating on Take-Two even as it slashed near-term estimates, and the reasoning behind that contradiction reveals just how much is riding on a single game release.
Published October 13, 2026, 1:55pm ET · 3 min read
Market Movers desk. Editor: David Moadel.
Take-Two Interactive Software (NASDAQ:TTWO | TTWO Price Prediction) stock is at $197.72, down 5% midday and off 23% year to date. Behind the drop is a Wells Fargo (NYSE:WFC) note that trimmed near-term estimates, and the selling looks company-specific because the rest of the gaming group is barely moving.
Gaming names around Take-Two tell a calmer story, and the contrast is sharp. Roblox (NYSE:RBLX) stock is flat at $49.60, holding steady even as Take-Two shares fall. Meanwhile, GameStop (NYSE:GME) stock is at $27.11, down 0.5%, a fraction of the move in Take-Two shares, and neither peer is responding to the Wells Fargo note.
The VanEck Video Gaming and eSports ETF (NASDAQ:ESPO) is flat, even though Take-Two represented 6.9% of the fund’s net assets as of June 30. For a wider benchmark, the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSEARCA:SPY) is down 0.1%, leaving Take-Two stock moving largely on its own.
Wells Fargo Cuts Near-Term Numbers but Keeps Its Overweight Call
Wells Fargo reiterated an Overweight rating and a $300 price target on Take-Two stock in the prior session. Beneath that headline, Wells Fargo trimmed its near-term bookings and adjusted EBITDA (earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization) estimates on weaker unit assumptions for the basketball franchise. Separately, Wells Fargo cut its recurrent consumer spending growth assumption on mixed player feedback to new gameplay mechanics and said Take-Two’s mobile business remains under pressure.
Looking ahead, Wells Fargo expects Take-Two’s third-quarter fiscal 2027 bookings and adjusted EBITDA guidance to come in below consensus. The rating and target remained unchanged. That is because of a Grand Theft Auto VI unit assumption that Wells Fargo places well above what it reads as implied in Take-Two’s current fiscal-year guidance. That gap is the whole debate in miniature: a weaker bridge to the release, paired with a bigger payoff once it arrives.
Gaming Group Holds Steady as Take-Two Falls Alone
Take-Two publishes the Grand Theft Auto and basketball franchises alongside a mobile portfolio, so its results turn on a few large releases and recurrent spending inside them. Roblox runs a user-generated platform, while GameStop is a specialty retailer. Each peer follows its own calendar, which keeps read-across inside this group weak.
Selling in Take-Two shares reflects a repricing ahead of a quarter Wells Fargo expects to guide below consensus, and with the VanEck fund and Roblox stock both flat, the evidence points back to the note itself.
What supports Take-Two is that the firm cutting near-term numbers kept both its rating and its target, because what it expects from Grand Theft Auto VI dwarfs the quarters in front of it. Rockstar Games, the Take-Two label behind the series, opened pre-orders in late June, and the game is scheduled to launch on November 19.
However, the bear case centers on the catalogue carrying Take-Two until that release, and both the basketball franchise and the mobile portfolio were marked down in a single Wells Fargo note, which suggests the path to launch is getting shakier. A softer bridge matters because Take-Two still reports another quarter before the release changes its results.
Take-Two’s next quarterly report lands in early November, on a date the company hasn’t confirmed, and that release is where the guidance Wells Fargo highlighted may surface. The open question is whether the pre-release catalogue holds firm enough to support the valuation until Grand Theft Auto VI ships.
The update is worth watching to see whether basketball unit trends and recurrent spending steady. Until then, TTWO shareholders may need to brace for more volatility around the report.

Take-Two shares could reach $300 as GTA VI upside remains unpriced, says Jefferies
Jefferies has reiterated its "buy" rating on Take-Two Interactive Software Inc (NASDAQ:TTWO), the video game publisher behind Grand Theft Auto, arguing that its shares could reach $300 as investors underestimate the potential of Grand Theft Auto VI.
The broker views the shares as attractive around $200, near their year-to-date lows, with a valuation of 20 times $12 in earnings per share for the year and a potential 50% upside to its price target.
Take-Two shares have fallen 17% since pre-orders opened for GTA VI, contrasting with an 18% gain during the comparable period before Red Dead Redemption 2 launched in 2018.
Jefferies argues that the market is already pricing in an outcome similar to the end of the Red Dead Redemption 2 launch cycle, despite additional growth opportunities that could distinguish GTA VI.
The broker's valuation comparison shows Take-Two trading at 20 times earnings for the second financial year ahead, below the 25 times multiple reached at a similar stage before Red Dead Redemption 2 was launched.
That valuation eventually fell to 20 times earnings by the end of 2018, when shares had retreated from their pre-launch peak and the Red Dead Online beta disappointed.
Jefferies believes the comparison understates GTA VI's potential because its online mode and a possible earlier personal computer release could generate additional sales and extend player engagement.
The broker maintains its forecast of $12 in earnings per share for the financial year 2028 and applies a 25 times earnings multiple to justifyfinancial year 2028 and applies a 25 times earnings multiple to support its $300 price target.
The potential timing of the PC version is a further reason for optimism, with GamesBeat reporting that industry sources expect it to arrive in the first quarter of calendar year 2027.
Jefferies cautions that the PC version has not been officially announced, but argues a release within months of the console launch would be significantly faster than previous Rockstar Games releases.
Red Dead Redemption 2 arrived on PC about 12 months after its console debut, while Grand Theft Auto V took roughly 19 months to make the transition.
An earlier PC release could also allow GTA VI's online mode to launch sooner, helping retain players after the initial excitement surrounding the console release begins to fade.
Jefferies sees particular potential in bringing PC players into the online environment early, including communities built around roleplaying modifications that have helped sustain the popularity of Grand Theft Auto V.
In a scenario where the PC version arrives during the fourth quarter of financial year 2027, Jefferies would cut its console sales forecast from 40 million units to 35 million.
However, the broker would add 12 million PC units, lifting projected GTA VI bookings for financial year 2027 from $2.5 billion to $2.9 billion.
The estimate includes revenue from premium editions, while Jefferies expects total bookings across the first 18 months to remain broadly unchanged or improve through an earlier contribution from the online mode.
The broker's central argument is that Take-Two's current valuation reflects a relatively cautious launch outcome, leaving investors exposed to potential upside if GTA VI's broader commercial ecosystem develops faster than expected.

Chicago, IL – October 15, 2026 – Today, Zacks Investment Ideas feature highlights Take-Two Interactive TTWO.
A Blockbuster Video Game Release Could Reignite This Stock
Take-Two Interactive has a major catalyst approaching, with its highly anticipated Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6) scheduled for release on November 19th. The title has generated massive excitement among gamers, and the blockbuster success of its predecessor suggests the release could be a major growth driver.
TTWO shares have struggled in 2026, but the upcoming release could easily reignite momentum.
Grand Theft Auto V, released more than a decade ago in 2013, was a huge success right out of the gate, generating more than $800 million in worldwide retail sales in its first 24 hours. The momentum continued, with sales surpassing the $1 billion mark in just three days.
And the success has extended well beyond the initial release, with Take-Two recently reporting that GTA 5 has now sold nearly 230 million copies worldwide. The continued demand more than a decade after its initial launch helps underpin the franchise's strong staying power.
Importantly, GTA Online has also been a major positive, allowing Take-Two to generate recurring revenue through in-game purchases and additional content long after the initial sale.
The upcoming release offers a massive opportunity for Take-Two, especially given the enormous installed fan base already built through GTA 5. Notably, the game is launching at $79.99, above the typical $59.99 price point seen when GTA 5 was initially released.
And the company's outlook already reflects expectations for a big boost, with management forecasting $8.0-$8.2 billion in net bookings for its current FY27, up considerably from the $6.72 billion reported in FY26. At the midpoint, the outlook suggests roughly 20% growth, with GTA 6 expected to be a primary driver of the acceleration.
Beyond the initial sales boost, the long-term opportunity also remains significant. GTA 5's continued success through GTA Online provides a strong blueprint for how Take-Two could monetize the new release for years, potentially creating a much higher recurring revenue base.
Our current consensus estimates for its FY27 and FY28 are reflective of a big growth acceleration relative to recent years, with earnings forecasted to climb 71% in its current FY27 (ends in March) and an additional 40% in FY28.
The valuation picture also isn't overstretched given the potential growth catalyst, with shares currently trading at a 24.4X forward 12-month earnings multiple, well beneath the 37.3X five-year median.
Take-Two Interactive has a major catalyst approaching with GTA 6, and the success of its predecessor suggests a new period of fresh growth. GTA 5's nearly 230 million lifetime copies sold and its ability to generate revenue more than a decade after release reflect the franchise's massive appeal. The stock deserves a close eye given the upcoming release and weak price action so far in 2026.

GameStop Pops 4% on Ryan Cohen’s Buying Binge; Take-Two Interactive and Roblox Advance 3%
Ryan Cohen keeps reaching into his own pocket to buy GameStop shares, and his conviction is pulling the entire gaming sector along for the ride. Here is what the insider buying pattern reveals about where GME could be headed.
Published September 30, 2026, 1:03pm ET · 3 min read
GameStop (NYSE:GME | GME Price Prediction) stock popped 4% to $24.79 on Wednesday, extending recent gains driven by Chairman and CEO Ryan Cohen’s continued open-market share purchases. Take-Two Interactive Software (NASDAQ:TTWO) shares advanced 3% to $209.78, while Roblox (NYSE:RBLX) stock also rose 3% to $42.53. Gaming-related names found support as attention remained focused on insider buying at GameStop.
The VanEck Video Gaming and eSports ETF (NASDAQ:ESPO) climbed 1% to $96.84. Broader markets moved higher, with the SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust (NYSE ARCA:SPY) up 0.52% to $768.20. GameStop’s latest headlines center on Ryan Cohen’s repeated buying, which has reinforced investor focus. The company recently reported a mixed quarter in which sales declined 19% while net income rose 77%, aided by cost cuts, collectibles growth, and investment gains, including from its eBay stake.
Ryan Cohen purchased 450,000 GameStop shares at approximately $23.48 each, for a total value of about $10.6 million, according to a recent SEC filing. The transaction follows earlier September purchases that included roughly 1.15 million shares for about $26.4 million and 1 million shares for about $20.4 million. Cohen’s direct holdings now stand near 41 million shares, representing roughly 8.8% of the company when including warrants.
These open-market buys form part of a broader pattern of insider accumulation throughout the year with no reported sales. The activity has helped sustain attention on GameStop shares even as the traditional video-game hardware and software business faces ongoing pressure.
Take-Two Interactive and Roblox Also Advance
Take-Two Interactive stock posted a solid gain. The company develops and publishes major interactive entertainment titles across console, PC, and mobile platforms. Take-Two Interactive shares have responded to both sector sentiment and its own pipeline developments in recent sessions.
Roblox stock moved higher as well. Roblox operates a platform that allows users to create and share immersive experiences, generating revenue primarily through in-platform purchases. Both Take-Two Interactive and Roblox operate in the broader gaming ecosystem but differ from GameStop’s retail and collectibles-focused model.
The VanEck Video Gaming and eSports ETF’s advance reflected measured strength across the niche. GameStop’s second-quarter results showed net sales of $790.2 million, down 19% year over year, while net income rose 77% to $298.7 million. Collectibles sales grew sharply and now account for a larger share of the mix, helped by cost discipline and non-operating gains tied to the company’s investment portfolio.
Similarities among GameStop, Take-Two Interactive, and Roblox include exposure to consumer spending on entertainment and digital content. Differences appear in business models, with GameStop emphasizing physical retail, collectibles, and balance-sheet management, while the other two focus on content creation and platform engagement. Insider conviction and a larger cash and investment position remain central to the GameStop narrative.
Ryan Cohen’s repeated purchases have provided a clear catalyst for GameStop stock in recent weeks. The mixed quarterly results highlight progress on profitability and mix shift even as top-line challenges persist. Strategic interest around the eBay investment and ongoing cost management continue to factor into investor discussions.
Investors should consider keeping position sizes modest given the elevated volatility that has long characterized GameStop stock. Further insider buying, sustained collectibles momentum, or clearer progress on strategic initiatives could support the shares, while weaker sales trends or shifts in retail sentiment may renew pressure across the group.

Grand Theft Auto VI Is Weeks Away. Is Take-Two Interactive (TTWO) Still a Buy at a Discount?
A video game company sitting on the most anticipated release in years would seem to deserve a premium price tag. Yet Take-Two Interactive Software (NASDAQ:TTWO) trades at a lower multiple than it has averaged over the past five years, with Grand Theft Auto VI only weeks away.
Take-Two owns Rockstar Games, the studio behind Grand Theft Auto and Red Dead Redemption, along with 2K's NBA 2K series and Zynga's mobile titles like Toon Blast and Words With Friends. It earns money when people buy its games, and even more from what they keep spending afterward on virtual currency, add-ons, and in-game items. Even with that lucrative pipeline, the video game publisher doesn't secure a spot among the 10 Best Undervalued Stocks to Buy in October. That leaves investors with a puzzle. Is the market underrating the biggest launch in the company's history, or quietly pricing in softness elsewhere in the portfolio? The answer depends on what happens after the launch-day buzz fades.
Is Cameco (CCJ) a Buy Before the Westinghouse Spin-Off?
Take-Two's real edge isn't one game. It's a catalog players keep returning to. In the fiscal first quarter of 2027, which ended in June, recurrent consumer spending made up 84% of net bookings (sales measured before accounting deferrals). That's money from people who already own the games and keep paying to play them.
The company's list of top contributors reads like a roll call of long-running franchises: NBA 2K, Grand Theft Auto, Red Dead Redemption, and mobile staples such as Toon Blast, Match Factory!, and Empires & Puzzles. Many of these are years old and still among its biggest earners. Annual sports releases run on that same repeat-spending model, which a major rival sports-game publisher depends on as well.
The fiscal first quarter wasn't a blowout. Net bookings slipped 3% to $1.39 billion, though that still landed slightly above management's guidance range. GAAP net revenue edged up to $1.53 billion from $1.50 billion, while the company posted a GAAP net loss of $34.1 million, or $0.18 per share.
The outlook is where the story lives. Management reiterated its fiscal 2027 target of $8.0 billion to $8.2 billion in net bookings, with GTA VI scheduled to arrive in November on PS5 and Xbox Series X|S. CEO Strauss Zelnick said the company expects to sustain this new level of scale and generate strong cash flows. Even with that historic growth trajectory on the horizon, the video game publisher remains noticeably absent from the 10 Best Growth Stocks to Buy Now According to Billionaires. Put that full-year target next to a $1.39 billion quarter, and it's obvious how much rides on the holiday months. CNBC reported that a recent preview of the game pointed to blockbuster demand.
What If Mobile Keeps Sliding?
The strongest objection sits in Take-Two's largest platform. Mobile net bookings fell to $739.5 million from $792.8 million, still accounting for 53% of the total. Console net revenue moved the other way, climbing to $640.5 million from $550.6 million.
That split matters. GTA VI launches on consoles, so a shrinking mobile business would leave Take-Two leaning harder on a single franchise. It's a pressure other mobile-heavy game makers have felt too. Recurrent spending dipped only 1%, so the engine underneath hasn't stalled. But mobile is the piece to watch once the launch excitement settles.
At a forward P/E of 31.05, as of October 12, investors are paying about $31 for every $1 of expected earnings. That's far below Take-Two's 5-year average P/E of 51.25, even as the company heads into the biggest product cycle in its history. It still looks pricey next to the sector P/E of 12.29. But few companies in that group are staring at a growth spike like this one. Analysts expect EPS growth of 49.70% in 2028, a pace that makes a sector-average multiple a poor fit.
There's an accounting wrinkle, too. GAAP guidance for fiscal 2027 calls for just $0.55 to $0.75 per share, so today's valuation rests on the earnings investors expect after GTA VI ships, not on this year's accounting profit. That's a bet on execution, and a big one.
Here's the tension, then. A stock that historically commanded more than 50 times earnings now sits near 31 right before its defining release. Either the market doubts the GTA VI surge will last, or it's leaving room for upside if players keep spending long after launch. That valuation gap highlights how much the market demands proven, long-tail monetization, the kind seen when Tencent Music (TME) turns streaming into a sprawling entertainment machine, rather than relying entirely on a single console release window. Hedge fund interest has risen, with 84 funds holding the stock in the most recent quarter, up from 77 in the prior one. Short interest sits at 4.45% of float, suggesting relatively limited bearish positioning.
The evidence points to a stock priced for a big launch, but not necessarily a lasting one. At roughly 31 times expected earnings, well under its own five-year norm, Take-Two looks reasonably valued if GTA VI keeps players spending for years, the way its predecessor did.
The setup suits patient investors comfortable with a hit-driven business and willing to sit through launch-quarter volatility. Would the picture change? Another delay, or mobile declines deep enough to swallow the console gains, would make even this discounted multiple harder to defend
While we acknowledge the risk and potential of TTWO as an investment, our conviction lies in the belief that some AI stocks hold greater promise for delivering higher returns and doing so within a shorter time frame. Proven product leader to advance Forma industry cloud and AI strategy and drive the next phase of AEC growth
SAN FRANCISCO, Oct. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Autodesk, Inc. (NASDAQ: ADSK) today announced that Diana Colella has been named executive vice president of its architecture, engineering and construction (AEC) business. Colella succeeds Amy Bunszel, who previously announced her retirement and will remain with Autodesk through November 2, 2026, to support the transition.
Colella will lead Autodesk's largest industry business as the company enters its next phase of growth in AEC, driven by Autodesk Forma, the company's industry cloud for AEC that connects data, context and workflows to deliver AI and project intelligence across the AEC lifecycle.
"The AEC industry is entering a new era, as AI creates new possibilities for how buildings and infrastructure are designed, built and operated," said Andrew Anagnost, president and CEO of Autodesk. "Amy and the AEC team have built a strong business and laid the foundation for the next phase of growth, with Forma becoming the industry cloud for AEC and AI helping customers navigate increasing complexity across the project lifecycle. Diana is the right leader for this moment. She brings a proven track record of leading through major technology shifts, aligning products, data and teams behind a clear vision, and turning innovation into tangible customer outcomes. Combined with her deep understanding of Autodesk and the industries we serve, Diana is uniquely positioned to build on this momentum and help shape the future of AEC."
p>In her new role, Colella will advance the Forma strategy while continuing to evolve our desktop products such as Revit and Civil 3D while connecting them more closely to Forma workflows. By bringing together the data and context created across the project lifecycle, Autodesk aims to make AI more useful in the work customers do every day, helping teams reduce friction, make better-informed decisions and increase their capacity to design and build.
Colella brings nearly three decades of Autodesk leadership experience spanning finance, strategy, sales, operations, product management and industry leadership. She joined Autodesk through the acquisition of Discreet Logic and has since held leadership roles across the company, including leading Autodesk's AutoCAD business and helping launch One AutoCAD. Her broad experience has given her deep insight into how Autodesk's products, operations and go-to-market teams work together to create customer success.
Most recently, Colella led the AI transformation of Autodesk's Media & Entertainment (M&E) business, where she advanced the Flow platform strategy and expanded Autodesk's role across the production lifecycle. Through acquisitions including Moxion, PIX and Wonder Dynamics, and the continued development of Autodesk Flow Studio, she helped broaden the value Autodesk delivers to creators and studios. Colella will continue to oversee the M&E business and will open a search for a new leader, reporting directly to her.
"Our customers are being asked to deliver more while navigating greater complexity, persistent resource constraints and rapid technological change," said Colella. "My priority is to listen to them, build on the strong foundation Amy and the team have created, and make sure the work we're doing across Forma and AI translates into meaningful improvements in how projects are designed, built and operated. I'm honored to lead Autodesk's AEC business at such an important moment for our customers and the industry."
The world's designers, engineers, builders, and creators trust Autodesk to help them design and make anything. From the buildings we live and work in, to the cars we drive and the bridges we drive over. From the products we use and rely on, to the movies and games that inspire us. Autodesk (ADSK) vs. PTC and TRMB: Can Cloud and AI Investments Drive Faster Earnings Growth?
Wed, October 14, 2026 at 11:43 AM CDT 7 min read
Is ADSK a good stock to buy? We came across a bullish thesis on Autodesk, Inc. on Astute Optics - US's Substack. The thesis was published on September 11th, when the stock was trading at $212.40, and ADSK gained 9.95% since then. The gain appears to reflect optimism around Autodesk's new AI capabilities and renewed takeover interest in design software following Schneider Electric's announced acquisition of PTC. In this article, we will summarize the bulls' thesis on ADSK. Autodesk, Inc.'s share was trading at $233.54 as of October 12th 2026. ADSK's trailing and forward P/E were 28.45 and 17.61 respectively according to Yahoo Finance.
This isn't the first time we see a software company pitched as a great investment. Software stocks have suffered steep declines over the past year, but does ADSK's recent recovery make this a good time to buy?
Shutterstock (SSTK) Unveils AI-Powered Creative Platform Evolution
In June, we published an article about the 10 Oversold Stocks Offering High Upside and ADSK ranked #7 in that article. Btw, the #1 stock in that list returned 29.89% since then. So, hedge funds were right about their #1 pick and ADSK rewarded their bullish stance with a 25.21% gain over the same period. This article explains why hedge funds were bullish on ADSK. Before getting into our analysis, let's take a look at the business and why some investors like the stock so much.
Autodesk, Inc. (NASDAQ:ADSK) provides 3D design, engineering, construction, manufacturing, and entertainment software through products such as AutoCAD, Revit, Autodesk Construction Cloud, Fusion, and Maya. Its shift toward cloud-based tools and artificial intelligence matters because these products are becoming more deeply built into how architects, engineers, manufacturers, and construction firms work.

Read More: Undervalued AI Stock Poised For Massive Gains: 10000% Upside Potential
Revenue climbed 17.9% year over year to $7.8 billion, and Autodesk runs a highly profitable business, with a 92.5% gross margin, a 21.1% net margin, and a strong 36.9% return on equity. Even so, the stock trades at about 25 times forward earnings, a valuation that assumes steady subscription growth continues, leaving little room for setbacks like weaker construction spending, slower manufacturing activity, or fewer new customer sign-ups.
The bullish case is that Autodesk is becoming harder for customers to leave, as Revit, Fusion, and Autodesk Construction Cloud shift toward shared, cloud-based platforms. Instead of using separate desktop software, customers can now collaborate around one central project, which raises switching costs and gives Autodesk more room to sell additional products into its existing customer base. At the same time, AI-driven design tools could make customers more productive and support further growth within larger accounts. Autodesk's already-high margins and strong returns suggest real operating leverage — meaning profits could grow faster than revenue — as long as subscriptions, renewals, and enterprise expansion keep holding up.
Management is backing this strategy with a 7% workforce reduction, cutting about 1,000 jobs, and redirecting that spending toward cloud infrastructure and AI. Autodesk is also changing how it sells software: rather than resellers handling the full transaction, deals will now settle directly between Autodesk and the customer, giving the company more control over renewals and pricing. Financially, Autodesk generated about $2.4 billion in free cash flow last fiscal year and holds roughly $677 million more cash than debt, giving it flexibility to keep investing. For next fiscal year, management expects earnings per share between $7.89 and $8.72, and the company has beaten Wall Street's profit estimates in each of its last four quarters.
Wall Street's average price target of $315.37, based on 34 analysts, implies the stock could rise about 53% from its current price of $206.62. But reaching that target would mean Autodesk trading at nearly 38 times earnings, well above its current 25 times multiple. For the stock to hit $315.37 while keeping today's valuation steady, earnings per share would need to jump to around $12.67 — about 64% higher than current levels. Since profits aren't yet close to that mark, investors should watch whether earnings growth accelerates enough to justify that kind of price target. You can check out why Berenberg sees more upside in Autodesk despite key AI headwinds here.
The biggest risk is a slowdown in commercial real estate, construction, or manufacturing. Higher borrowing costs can delay building projects and reduce new construction starts, which would slow demand for Autodesk's design software, while weaker industrial activity could cause manufacturers to pull back spending too. The company also carries more debt than equity, and its current ratio of 0.85 means it has fewer short-term assets than short-term liabilities, leaving a thinner cushion despite its net cash position. Deeper cloud adoption also raises cybersecurity risk, since Autodesk's software often stores sensitive architectural and infrastructure designs. On top of that, cheaper CAD software in China and competitors like Bentley Systems Incorporated (NASDAQ:BSY) add pricing pressure in some markets. Together, these risks leave little room for error if growth slows.
Another risk for the stock is that its new sales model could make revenue growth look stronger than the underlying business. Autodesk now records partner incentives as operating costs rather than deductions from revenue. This raises reported revenue without necessarily bringing in more customer spending. Autodesk says the change boosts calculated revenue growth while being broadly neutral to operating profit and free cash flow. Its valuation depends on genuine subscription growth and stronger earnings. Investors could overestimate that growth if they mistake accounting changes for increased demand. In our opinion, this could pressure Autodesk's price multiples if profit growth fails to match the headline revenue gains.
Hedge fund positioning shows a mixed signal. As per our database, 51 hedge funds held Autodesk at the end of the second quarter, down from 67 in the previous quarter. That pullback suggests institutional investors turned more cautious on Autodesk despite its strong profitability and long-term growth potential. By comparison, PTC Inc. (NASDAQ:PTC) was held by 45 hedge funds, up from 42, Bentley Systems Incorporated was held by 31 hedge funds, down from 38, and Trimble Inc. (NASDAQ:TRMB) was held by 46 hedge funds, up from 43. Institutional sentiment cooled more sharply toward Autodesk than toward its peers this quarter, even though Autodesk still held the highest total hedge fund ownership among the four companies.
Short interest data paints a relatively calm picture. Only 5.01% of Autodesk's float is sold short, well below PTC Inc. at 8.49% and Bentley Systems Incorporated at 7.95%, though slightly above Trimble Inc. at 4.89%. So even though hedge fund ownership fell, bearish bets against Autodesk remain lower than those against PTC and Bentley Systems — suggesting the debate around the stock centers less on the business deteriorating and more on whether its growth and margins can support its valuation.
ADSK's forward P/E is 17.61x. PTC Inc., Bentley Systems Incorporated, and Trimble Inc. trade at forward P/Es of 16.26x, 19.96x, and 13.97x, respectively. ADSK's own forward P/E was 22.17x on January 31, 2026, putting its current valuation approximately 21% below that level. We believe the current valuation reflects investor concerns about weaker construction and manufacturing demand, competition, and whether cloud and AI investments will deliver stronger profits. However, the lower multiple makes Autodesk more attractive against its own history, while its premium to PTC and Trimble still requires dependable earnings growth. Autodesk, Inc.'s adjusted earnings per share increased from $6.63 in fiscal 2023 to $10.43 in fiscal 2026, representing approximately 16% annual growth. We believe 17.61 times expected earnings is a reasonable valuation if growth continues near that pace, because rising profits could support share-price gains without investors needing to pay a higher multiple. If Autodesk can maintain subscription growth and turn cost savings into lasting profits, the current valuation could offer an attractive entry point despite the risks from weaker customer spending and competition.
Previously, we covered a bullish thesis on Autodesk, Inc. (ADSK) by Francesco Ferrari in March 2025, which highlighted the company's 93% recurring revenue, 92% gross margin, and strong free cash flow generation. ADSK's stock price has depreciated by approximately 5.98% since our coverage. We believe ADSK could be a good long-term investment, provided continued subscription growth and improving profitability justify its current valuation.
Autodesk, Inc. is not on our list of the 40 Most Popular Stocks Among Hedge Funds. While ADSK could offer long-term upside if growing cloud subscriptions and AI-powered design tools drive stronger earnings, we believe some AI stocks offer stronger long-term potential, with a high probability of delivering superior returns on a much shorter timeline.
