Is Autodesk (ADSK) Below Fair Value As Its New AEC Chief Pushes AI And Cloud?
Autodesk (ADSK) just reshuffled a key leadership seat, putting long-time executive Diana Colella in charge of its architecture, engineering and construction business as investors watch how this affects the company's push into AI and cloud tools.
Autodesk shares trade at US$233.60, with a 7 day share price return of 10.55% and a 30 day gain of 10.08%. However, the year to date share price return is down 18.53% and the 1 year total shareholder return has declined 24.72%, so recent momentum is rebuilding from a weaker longer run patch as investors weigh leadership changes and new AI partnerships.

Autodesk now trades well below both analyst targets and some intrinsic value estimates after that sharp rebound. Is this discount a reasonable response to growth concerns, or is the market mispricing the AI and cloud story?
At a last close of $233.60, the most followed narrative around Autodesk points to a fair value of $370 per share. This frames the current leadership reshuffle and AI push against a much higher long term anchor.
At roughly $212 against a certified value around $370, the market seems to be pricing a meaningful amount of AI damage before the customer numbers show it. Maybe the market is early. Maybe I'm wrong. But that is exactly what margin of safety is for.

According to John_Eric, that margin of safety view leans heavily on Autodesk converting an already scaled subscription base into durable free cash flow, while treating AI as a risk to seat economics rather than a verdict on the whole platform. The narrative also flags that analysts as a group still see upside, with a consensus price target of $307.54, and internal fair value work that places Autodesk about 36.9% below an estimated $370 level.
The story is not one way. Autodesk earnings have grown 11.1% per year over the past 5 years and 57.4% in the most recent year, yet forecast revenue growth of 9.8% per year and profit growth of 13.4% per year sit behind the wider US market expectations of 13.9% and 17.7% respectively. That mix of solid historical performance, slower projected expansion compared to the broader market, and a share price that has fallen 24.72% over the past year while underperforming both the US market and the US Software sector, is exactly what gives this valuation debate its edge.
Autodesk also shows some quality markers that feature prominently in the narrative. Net profit margins of 21.1% are higher than last year's 15.8%, return on equity is described as outstanding at 48.54% albeit flattered by higher leverage, and earnings are assessed as high quality. At the same time, the financing structure relies entirely on higher risk sources of funding such as external borrowing, and revenue is expected to expand slower than 20% per year, so this is not a simple high growth story that investors can set and forget.
On price signals, several tools line up with the underpriced thesis. Autodesk is trading 31.7% below the average analyst target, about 32.1% under one fair value estimate, and below an SWS DCF model output that puts future cash flow value at $343.92 per share. P/E of 29.7x screens as broadly in line with the wider US Software group at 30.4x, although it comes in higher than a narrower peer set on 19.2x, and close to an estimated fair P/E of 31.8x. That mix suggests the multiple is not unusually stretched for a business with 57.4% recent earnings growth and 13.36% projected profit expansion, even after a year where the stock has lagged the sector.
For investors weighing the leadership change and AI partnerships, the narrative effectively asks whether recent share price weakness already reflects a fair amount of AI related risk to seat counts, pricing power, and long term free cash flow, given the current fundamentals. It also raises governance and execution questions, such as Autodesk bringing on 5 new directors in three years, CEO compensation of $30.09m that runs above the US large cap average, and a board and management team that are described as experienced with more than 4 years of average tenure. Those details shape how much confidence investors may place in Autodesk's ability to capture AI driven productivity upside economically rather than leaving it entirely with customers.

Autodesk names Diana Colella to lead architecture, engineering and construction business
Proven product leader to advance Forma industry cloud and AI strategy and drive the next phase of AEC growth
SAN FRANCISCO, Oct. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Autodesk, Inc. (NASDAQ: ADSK) today announced that Diana Colella has been named executive vice president of its architecture, engineering and construction (AEC) business. Colella succeeds Amy Bunszel, who previously announced her retirement and will remain with Autodesk through November 2, 2026, to support the transition.
Colella will lead Autodesk's largest industry business as the company enters its next phase of growth in AEC, driven by Autodesk Forma, the company's industry cloud for AEC that connects data, context and workflows to deliver AI and project intelligence across the AEC lifecycle.
"The AEC industry is entering a new era, as AI creates new possibilities for how buildings and infrastructure are designed, built and operated," said Andrew Anagnost, president and CEO of Autodesk. "Amy and the AEC team have built a strong business and laid the foundation for the next phase of growth, with Forma becoming the industry cloud for AEC and AI helping customers navigate increasing complexity across the project lifecycle. Diana is the right leader for this moment. She brings a proven track record of leading through major technology shifts, aligning products, data and teams behind a clear vision, and turning innovation into tangible customer outcomes. Combined with her deep understanding of Autodesk and the industries we serve, Diana is uniquely positioned to build on this momentum and help shape the future of AEC."
In her new role, Colella will advance the Forma strategy while continuing to evolve our desktop products such as Revit and Civil 3D while connecting them more closely to Forma workflows. By bringing together the data and context created across the project lifecycle, Autodesk aims to make AI more useful in the work customers do every day, helping teams reduce friction, make better-informed decisions and increase their capacity to design and build.
Colella brings nearly three decades of Autodesk leadership experience spanning finance, strategy, sales, operations, product management and industry leadership. She joined Autodesk through the acquisition of Discreet Logic and has since held leadership roles across the company, including leading Autodesk's AutoCAD business and helping launch One AutoCAD. Her broad experience has given her deep insight into how Autodesk's products, operations and go-to-market teams work together to create customer success.
Most recently, Colella led the AI transformation of Autodesk's Media & Entertainment (M&E) business, where she advanced the Flow platform strategy and expanded Autodesk's role across the production lifecycle. Through acquisitions including Moxion, PIX and Wonder Dynamics, and the continued development of Autodesk Flow Studio, she helped broaden the value Autodesk delivers to creators and studios. Colella will continue to oversee the M&E business and will open a search for a new leader, reporting directly to her.
"Our customers are being asked to deliver more while navigating greater complexity, persistent resource constraints and rapid technological change," said Colella. "My priority is to listen to them, build on the strong foundation Amy and the team have created, and make sure the work we're doing across Forma and AI translates into meaningful improvements in how projects are designed, built and operated. I'm honored to lead Autodesk's AEC business at such an important moment for our customers and the industry."
The world's designers, engineers, builders, and creators trust Autodesk to help them design and make anything. From the buildings we live and work in, to the cars we drive and the bridges we drive over. From the products we use and rely on, to the movies and games that inspire us. Autodesk's Design and Make Platform unlocks the power of data to accelerate insights and automate processes, empowering customers with the technology to create the world around us and deliver better outcomes for their businesses and the planet. Is Autodesk Still The Best Way To Own Faster Software Growth?
Thu, October 15, 2026 at 5:52 PM CDT 4 min read
Autodesk (ADSK) stock lost 24.9% over the past year, while shares of Fair Isaac (FICO) fell 56.4%. Underneath those market declines, however, business at both software companies is accelerating. Each firm has posted faster sales growth in each of the past two years, and buyers of either stock are likely betting on that continued momentum. The similarities end there. The two companies operate with completely different financial structures. Fair Isaac retains far more of its sales as profit, yet Autodesk carries substantially less debt. So which of the two does the evidence favor?
In August, Autodesk Gave A Mixed Outlook
On August 27, Autodesk adjusted its expectations for the fiscal year ending in January 2027. The company raised its revenue forecast to a midpoint of $8.32 billion, up from $8.19 billion, and also increased its billings forecast. At the same time, it lowered its reported operating margin forecast down to 26.0% at the midpoint, from 27.0%.
Fair Isaac delivered a uniformly positive update on July 29, 2026. The company raised every forecast it gave for revenue, net income and earnings per share. For the fiscal year that ended in September 2026, management guided for $2.53 billion in revenue. Final results for that period are still to come.
Those optimistic projections arrived two months before a major industry announcement.
On September 28, the Federal Housing Finance Agency said the mortgage pricing grid is being simplified and that VantageScore is being incorporated. Fair Isaac stock fell after that statement the next day.
Autodesk Keeps Less Of Each Dollar, Holds More Cash
Looking at profitability, the two businesses operate in different tiers. Autodesk turned 27.9% of its sales into operating profit over the twelve months to July 2026. By contrast, Fair Isaac converted 52.1% of its sales into operating profit over the twelve months to June 2026.
When evaluating the balance sheet, Autodesk holds a commanding advantage. As of July 31, 2026, the company held $4.16 billion in cash and short-term investments, which easily exceeded its $3.71 billion of debt. Fair Isaac sits in a much tighter position. At June 30, 2026, the company owed $5.6 billion in debt against just $248 million of cash and short-term investments.
Fair Isaac trades at a notable discount relative to its bottom line. The stock trades at 20.0 times its earnings over the past twelve months. Investors are paying a higher premium for Autodesk, which trades at 29.6 times trailing earnings.
The top line also favors Fair Isaac. The company expanded sales by 24.1% over the twelve months to June 2026, easily outpacing the 17.9% growth Autodesk recorded over the twelve months to July 2026. Expanding the timeline reveals a similar pattern. Over its last three twelve-month periods, Fair Isaac averaged 17.7% growth, compared to 14.4% for Autodesk.
Autodesk reclaims the advantage regarding debt. The company carries debt equal to 7.6% of its market value. That sits well below the 34.4% ratio for Fair Isaac.
Based on its earnings multiple, growth, margin and forecasts, Fair Isaac comes out ahead, while Autodesk owes far less. The key variable remains timing. Fair Isaac issued its results and forecasts entirely before the agency's September move. The company expects to release its first report since that development on or around November 11, 2026. You should watch what Fair Isaac says about revenue in that report.

Tech stocks broadly declined this week as escalating tensions over the Iran war fueled fresh uncertainty across financial markets.
Traders work on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange during morning trading on August 05, 2026. (Photo by Michael M. Santiago/Getty Images)
Autodesk gains momentum after Schneider Electric’s $22.6 billion deal for PTC sparks fresh interest in industrial software firms.
Intuit rebounds after management signals confidence in the company’s underlying value and halts planned executive stock sales.
Analyst price targets suggest roughly 32% upside for Autodesk and 33% for Intuit, despite mixed retail sentiment.

Autodesk Inc. (ADSK) and Intuit Inc. (INTU) are heading for their strongest weekly performances in months, bucking a broader market downturn and signaling renewed optimism about the sector’s growth prospects.
ADSK stock climbed around 10% so far this week, while Intuit gained approximately 8%, putting both among the Nasdaq 100’s top 10 gainers. The rally comes as the Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ), which tracks the Nasdaq 100, slipped around 0.3% over the same period.

Autodesk’s rally gathered momentum after Schneider Electric agreed to acquire industrial software maker PTC Inc. (PTC) in an all-cash deal valued at approximately $22.6 billion, or $205 per share. The offer represented a 42.3% premium to PTC’s previous closing price.
The acquisition appears to have prompted investors to reassess valuations across the engineering and industrial software sector, where Autodesk also operates.

Autodesk names Diana Colella to lead architecture, engineering and construction business
Autodesk names Diana Colella to lead architecture, engineering and construction business
Proven product leader to advance Forma industry cloud and AI strategy and drive the next phase of AEC growth
SAN FRANCISCO, Oct. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Autodesk, Inc. (NASDAQ: ADSK) today announced that Diana Colella has been named executive vice president of its architecture, engineering and construction (AEC) business. Colella succeeds Amy Bunszel, who previously announced her retirement and will remain with Autodesk through November 2, 2026, to support the transition.
Colella will lead Autodesk's largest industry business as the company enters its next phase of growth in AEC, driven by Autodesk Forma, the company's industry cloud for AEC that connects data, context and workflows to deliver AI and project intelligence across the AEC lifecycle.
"The AEC industry is entering a new era, as AI creates new possibilities for how buildings and infrastructure are designed, built and operated," said Andrew Anagnost, president and CEO of Autodesk. "Amy and the AEC team have built a strong business and laid the foundation for the next phase of growth, with Forma becoming the industry cloud for AEC and AI helping customers navigate increasing complexity across the project lifecycle. Diana is the right leader for this moment. She brings a proven track record of leading through major technology shifts, aligning products, data and teams behind a clear vision, and turning innovation into tangible customer outcomes. Combined with her deep understanding of Autodesk and the industries we serve, Diana is uniquely positioned to build on this momentum and help shape the future of AEC."
p>In her new role, Colella will advance the Forma strategy while continuing to evolve our desktop products such as Revit and Civil 3D while connecting them more closely to Forma workflows. By bringing together the data and context created across the project lifecycle, Autodesk aims to make AI more useful in the work customers do every day, helping teams reduce friction, make better-informed decisions and increase their capacity to design and build.
Colella brings nearly three decades of Autodesk leadership experience spanning finance, strategy, sales, operations, product management and industry leadership. She joined Autodesk through the acquisition of Discreet Logic and has since held leadership roles across the company, including leading Autodesk's AutoCAD business and helping launch One AutoCAD. Her broad experience has given her deep insight into how Autodesk's products, operations and go-to-market teams work together to create customer success.
Most recently, Colella led the AI transformation of Autodesk's Media & Entertainment (M&E) business, where she advanced the Flow platform strategy and expanded Autodesk's role across the production lifecycle. Through acquisitions including Moxion, PIX and Wonder Dynamics, and the continued development of Autodesk Flow Studio, she helped broaden the value Autodesk delivers to creators and studios. Colella will continue to oversee the M&E business and will open a search for a new leader, reporting directly to her.
"Our customers are being asked to deliver more while navigating greater complexity, persistent resource constraints and rapid technological change," said Colella. "My priority is to listen to them, build on the strong foundation Amy and the team have created, and make sure the work we're doing across Forma and AI translates into meaningful improvements in how projects are designed, built and operated. I'm honored to lead Autodesk's AEC business at such an important moment for our customers and the industry."
The world's designers, engineers, builders, and creators trust Autodesk to help them design and make anything. From the buildings we live and work in, to the cars we drive and the bridges we drive over. From the products we use and rely on, to the movies and games that inspire us. Autodesk's Design and Make Platform unlocks the power of data to accelerate insights and automate processes, empowering customers with the technology to create the world around us and deliver better outcomes for their businesses and the planet. For more information, visit autodesk.com or follow @autodesk. #MakeAnything

Autodesk (ADSK) vs. PTC and TRMB: Can Cloud and AI Investments Drive Faster Earnings Growth?
Wed, October 14, 2026 at 11:43 AM CDT 7 min read
Is ADSK a good stock to buy? We came across a bullish thesis on Autodesk, Inc. on Astute Optics - US's Substack. The thesis was published on September 11th, when the stock was trading at $212.40, and ADSK gained 9.95% since then. The gain appears to reflect optimism around Autodesk's new AI capabilities and renewed takeover interest in design software following Schneider Electric's announced acquisition of PTC. In this article, we will summarize the bulls' thesis on ADSK. Autodesk, Inc.'s share was trading at $233.54 as of October 12th 2026. ADSK's trailing and forward P/E were 28.45 and 17.61 respectively according to Yahoo Finance.
This isn't the first time we see a software company pitched as a great investment. Software stocks have suffered steep declines over the past year, but does ADSK's recent recovery make this a good time to buy?
Shutterstock (SSTK) Unveils AI-Powered Creative Platform Evolution
In June, we published an article about the 10 Oversold Stocks Offering High Upside and ADSK ranked #7 in that article. Btw, the #1 stock in that list returned 29.89% since then. So, hedge funds were right about their #1 pick and ADSK rewarded their bullish stance with a 25.21% gain over the same period. This article explains why hedge funds were bullish on ADSK. Before getting into our analysis, let's take a look at the business and why some investors like the stock so much.
Autodesk, Inc. (NASDAQ:ADSK) provides 3D design, engineering, construction, manufacturing, and entertainment software through products such as AutoCAD, Revit, Autodesk Construction Cloud, Fusion, and Maya. Its shift toward cloud-based tools and artificial intelligence matters because these products are becoming more deeply built into how architects, engineers, manufacturers, and construction firms work.
Read More: 15 AI Stocks That Are Quietly Making Investors Rich
Read More: Undervalued AI Stock Poised For Massive Gains: 10000% Upside Potential
Revenue climbed 17.9% year over year to $7.8 billion, and Autodesk runs a highly profitable business, with a 92.5% gross margin, a 21.1% net margin, and a strong 36.9% return on equity. Even so, the stock trades at about 25 times forward earnings, a valuation that assumes steady subscription growth continues, leaving little room for setbacks like weaker construction spending, slower manufacturing activity, or fewer new customer sign-ups.
The bullish case is that Autodesk is becoming harder for customers to leave, as Revit, Fusion, and Autodesk Construction Cloud shift toward shared, cloud-based platforms. Instead of using separate desktop software, customers can now collaborate around one central project, which raises switching costs and gives Autodesk more room to sell additional products into its existing customer base. At the same time, AI-driven design tools could make customers more productive and support further growth within larger accounts. Autodesk's already-high margins and strong returns suggest real operating leverage — meaning profits could grow faster than revenue — as long as subscriptions, renewals, and enterprise expansion keep holding up.
Management is backing this strategy with a 7% workforce reduction, cutting about 1,000 jobs, and redirecting that spending toward cloud infrastructure and AI. Autodesk is also changing how it sells software: rather than resellers handling the full transaction, deals will now settle directly between Autodesk and the customer, giving the company more control over renewals and pricing. Financially, Autodesk generated about $2.4 billion in free cash flow last fiscal year and holds roughly $677 million more cash than debt, giving it flexibility to keep investing. For next fiscal year, management expects earnings per share between $7.89 and $8.72, and the company has beaten Wall Street's profit estimates in each of its last four quarters.
Wall Street's average price target of $315.37, based on 34 analysts, implies the stock could rise about 53% from its current price of $206.62. But reaching that target would mean Autodesk trading at nearly 38 times earnings, well above its current 25 times multiple. For the stock to hit $315.37 while keeping today's valuation steady, earnings per share would need to jump to around $12.67 — about 64% higher than current levels. Since profits aren't yet close to that mark, investors should watch whether earnings growth accelerates enough to justify that kind of price target. You can check out why Berenberg sees more upside in Autodesk despite key AI headwinds here.
The biggest risk is a slowdown in commercial real estate, construction, or manufacturing. Higher borrowing costs can delay building projects and reduce new construction starts, which would slow demand for Autodesk's design software, while weaker industrial activity could cause manufacturers to pull back spending too. The company also carries more debt than equity, and its current ratio of 0.85 means it has fewer short-term assets than short-term liabilities, leaving a thinner cushion despite its net cash position. Deeper cloud adoption also raises cybersecurity risk, since Autodesk's software often stores sensitive architectural and infrastructure designs. On top of that, cheaper CAD software in China and competitors like Bentley Systems Incorporated (NASDAQ:BSY) add pricing pressure in some markets. Together, these risks leave little room for error if growth slows.
Another risk for the stock is that its new sales model could make revenue growth look stronger than the underlying business. Autodesk now records partner incentives as operating costs rather than deductions from revenue. This raises reported revenue without necessarily bringing in more customer spending. Autodesk says the change boosts calculated revenue growth while being broadly neutral to operating profit and free cash flow. Its valuation depends on genuine subscription growth and stronger earnings. Investors could overestimate that growth if they mistake accounting changes for increased demand. In our opinion, this could pressure Autodesk's price multiples if profit growth fails to match the headline revenue gains.
Hedge fund positioning shows a mixed signal. As per our database, 51 hedge funds held Autodesk at the end of the second quarter, down from 67 in the previous quarter. That pullback suggests institutional investors turned more cautious on Autodesk despite its strong profitability and long-term growth potential. By comparison, PTC Inc. (NASDAQ:PTC) was held by 45 hedge funds, up from 42, Bentley Systems Incorporated was held by 31 hedge funds, down from 38, and Trimble Inc. (NASDAQ:TRMB) was held by 46 hedge funds, up from 43. Institutional sentiment cooled more sharply toward Autodesk than toward its peers this quarter, even though Autodesk still held the highest total hedge fund ownership among the four companies.
Short interest data paints a relatively calm picture. Only 5.01% of Autodesk's float is sold short, well below PTC Inc. at 8.49% and Bentley Systems Incorporated at 7.95%, though slightly above Trimble Inc. at 4.89%. So even though hedge fund ownership fell, bearish bets against Autodesk remain lower than those against PTC and Bentley Systems — suggesting the debate around the stock centers less on the business deteriorating and more on whether its growth and margins can support its valuation.
ADSK's forward P/E is 17.61x. PTC Inc., Bentley Systems Incorporated, and Trimble Inc. trade at forward P/Es of 16.26x, 19.96x, and 13.97x, respectively. ADSK's own forward P/E was 22.17x on January 31, 2026, putting its current valuation approximately 21% below that level. We believe the current valuation reflects investor concerns about weaker construction and manufacturing demand, competition, and whether cloud and AI investments will deliver stronger profits. However, the lower multiple makes Autodesk more attractive against its own history, while its premium to PTC and Trimble still requires dependable earnings growth. Autodesk, Inc.'s adjusted earnings per share increased from $6.63 in fiscal 2023 to $10.43 in fiscal 2026, representing approximately 16% annual growth. We believe 17.61 times expected earnings is a reasonable valuation if growth continues near that pace, because rising profits could support share-price gains without investors needing to pay a higher multiple. If Autodesk can maintain subscription growth and turn cost savings into lasting profits, the current valuation could offer an attractive entry point despite the risks from weaker customer spending and competition.
Previously, we covered a bullish thesis on Autodesk, Inc. (ADSK) by Francesco Ferrari in March 2025, which highlighted the company's 93% recurring revenue, 92% gross margin, and strong free cash flow generation. ADSK's stock price has depreciated by approximately 5.98% since our coverage. We believe ADSK could be a good long-term investment, provided continued subscription growth and improving profitability justify its current valuation.
Autodesk, Inc. is not on our list of the 40 Most Popular Stocks Among Hedge Funds. While ADSK could offer long-term upside if growing cloud subscriptions and AI-powered design tools drive stronger earnings, we believe some AI stocks offer stronger long-term potential, with a high probability of delivering superior returns on a much shorter timeline. If you are looking for an AI stock that is more promising than ADSK and that has 10,000% upside potential, check out our report about this cheapest AI stock.

PTC (PTC) vs Autodesk (ADSK): Which is a Better Stock to Buy?
PTC Inc. (NASDAQ:PTC) traded at around $194 on October 7, little changed on the day and 4.32% lower over twelve months.
Autodesk, Inc. (NASDAQ:ADSK) traded near $235 over the same session, down 25.73% across the year. One of these two received a $22.6 billion cash bid last week and is still below where it traded a year ago.

PTC (PTC) vs Autodesk (ADSK): Which is a Better Stock to Buy?
The Company Being Bought Is the One That Shrank:
Revenue fell 6.80% at PTC in the most recent quarter while Autodesk grew 16.10%. Earnings tell the same story, down 16.00% against up 57.20%.
So Schneider Electric agreed to pay $22.6 billion in cash for the design software company whose revenue is going backwards.
Gross margins run 92.50% at Autodesk against 84.50% at PTC, which is the usual gap between a subscription base and a licensed one. Operating margins are close at 29.23% against 28.23%, so the difference is being spent rather than kept. Return on equity is 53.85% at Autodesk against 35.05%, and neither figure is held back by the operations. In January we ranked ten stocks for high returns. The one we put first has returned almost 30% since.
One Margin at PTC Does Not Come From Software:
Net margin at PTC is 41.43% and operating margin is 28.23%. Net margin above operating margin means profit arrived from below the operating line rather than from selling licences. The multiples carry the distortion. PTC trades at 18.72 times trailing earnings and 21.71 times forward.
A forward figure above the trailing one says this year's profit is not expected to repeat, which is the same fact stated as a forecast. Autodesk moves the other way, from 29.98 times trailing to 16.55 times forward. Return on assets is 11.54% at PTC against 11.47% at Autodesk, so the two use their asset bases almost identically.
Free cash flow settles the quality question. Autodesk generated $2.80 billion against $935.48 million at PTC. In May, we ranked this year's best dividend performers. The one that finished first has since fallen 38%.
The Valuation Case:
Sustainability for PTC is now a question for its acquirer rather than for the market, since the price is agreed. On price, Autodesk is the cheaper stock on forward estimates at 16.55 times against 21.71, with a PEG ratio of 0.78 against 1.81.
Enterprise value to EBITDA is closer at 17.45 for PTC against 21.29, because that measure counts the $1.61 billion of debt. Short interest of 9.21% at PTC against 4.45% is unusual for a company with an agreed cash offer on the table.
Conclusion:
Autodesk is the better business by every operating measure that matters. Revenue grew 16.10% against a 6.80% decline, earnings rose 57.20% against a 16.00% fall, and free cash flow of $2.80 billion is three times PTC's. However, PTC has an agreed $22.6 billion cash offer and Autodesk has nothing of the kind, which is why one fell 4.32% over twelve months and the other 25.73%. PTC's 41.43% net margin above a 28.23% operating margin is not repeatable. The number to watch is Autodesk's forward multiple, because 16.55 times is what the market pays for the grower nobody bid for.
Market Sentiment:
PTC Inc. (NASDAQ:PTC) was held by 45 hedge funds with a combined stake value of about $1.01 billion at the end of Q2 2026 in the Insider Monkey database. This is up from 42 hedge fund holders with a cumulative investment value of around $1.06 billion in the previous quarter.
Autodesk, Inc. (NASDAQ:ADSK) was held by 51 hedge funds with a combined stake value of about $2.28 billion at the end of Q2 2026 in the Insider Monkey database. This is down from 67 hedge fund holders with a cumulative investment value of around $3.17 billion in the previous quarter.

Is Autodesk (ADSK) Below Fair Value As Its New AEC Chief Pushes AI And Cloud?
Autodesk (ADSK) just reshuffled a key leadership seat, putting long-time executive Diana Colella in charge of its architecture, engineering and construction business as investors watch how this affects the company's push into AI and cloud tools.
Autodesk shares trade at US$233.60, with a 7 day share price return of 10.55% and a 30 day gain of 10.08%. However, the year to date share price return is down 18.53% and the 1 year total shareholder return has declined 24.72%, so recent momentum is rebuilding from a weaker longer run patch as investors weigh leadership changes and new AI partnerships.
Scan how Autodesk's AI and cloud push compares with peers by reviewing our hand picked list of 37 AI small caps.
Autodesk now trades well below both analyst targets and some intrinsic value estimates after that sharp rebound. Is this discount a reasonable response to growth concerns, or is the market mispricing the AI and cloud story?
At a last close of $233.60, the most followed narrative around Autodesk points to a fair value of $370 per share. This frames the current leadership reshuffle and AI push against a much higher long term anchor.
At roughly $212 against a certified value around $370, the market seems to be pricing a meaningful amount of AI damage before the customer numbers show it. Maybe the market is early. Maybe I'm wrong. But that is exactly what margin of safety is for.
See why 12 investors see Autodesk as 37% undervalued.
According to John_Eric, that margin of safety view leans heavily on Autodesk converting an already scaled subscription base into durable free cash flow, while treating AI as a risk to seat economics rather than a verdict on the whole platform. The narrative also flags that analysts as a group still see upside, with a consensus price target of $307.54, and internal fair value work that places Autodesk about 36.9% below an estimated $370 level.
The story is not one way. Autodesk earnings have grown 11.1% per year over the past 5 years and 57.4% in the most recent year, yet forecast revenue growth of 9.8% per year and profit growth of 13.4% per year sit behind the wider US market expectations of 13.9% and 17.7% respectively. That mix of solid historical performance, slower projected expansion compared to the broader market, and a share price that has fallen 24.72% over the past year while underperforming both the US market and the US Software sector, is exactly what gives this valuation debate its edge.
Autodesk also shows some quality markers that feature prominently in the narrative. Net profit margins of 21.1% are higher than last year's 15.8%, return on equity is described as outstanding at 48.54% albeit flattered by higher leverage, and earnings are assessed as high quality. At the same time, the financing structure relies entirely on higher risk sources of funding such as external borrowing, and revenue is expected to expand slower than 20% per year, so this is not a simple high growth story that investors can set and forget.
On price signals, several tools line up with the underpriced thesis. Autodesk is trading 31.7% below the average analyst target, about 32.1% under one fair value estimate, and below an SWS DCF model output that puts future cash flow value at $343.92 per share. P/E of 29.7x screens as broadly in line with the wider US Software group at 30.4x, although it comes in higher than a narrower peer set on 19.2x, and close to an estimated fair P/E of 31.8x. That mix suggests the multiple is not unusually stretched for a business with 57.4% recent earnings growth and 13.36% projected profit expansion, even after a year where the stock has lagged the sector.
For investors weighing the leadership change and AI partnerships, the narrative effectively asks whether recent share price weakness already reflects a fair amount of AI related risk to seat counts, pricing power, and long term free cash flow, given the current fundamentals. It also raises governance and execution questions, such as Autodesk bringing on 5 new directors in three years, CEO compensation of $30.09m that runs above the US large cap average, and a board and management team that are described as experienced with more than 4 years of average tenure. Those details shape how much confidence investors may place in Autodesk's ability to capture AI driven productivity upside economically rather than leaving it entirely with customers.

Autodesk names Diana Colella to lead architecture, engineering and construction business
Proven product leader to advance Forma industry cloud and AI strategy and drive the next phase of AEC growth
SAN FRANCISCO, Oct. 6, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Autodesk, Inc. (NASDAQ: ADSK) today announced that Diana Colella has been named executive vice president of its architecture, engineering and construction (AEC) business. Colella succeeds Amy Bunszel, who previously announced her retirement and will remain with Autodesk through November 2, 2026, to support the transition.
Colella will lead Autodesk's largest industry business as the company enters its next phase of growth in AEC, driven by Autodesk Forma, the company's industry cloud for AEC that connects data, context and workflows to deliver AI and project intelligence across the AEC lifecycle.
"The AEC industry is entering a new era, as AI creates new possibilities for how buildings and infrastructure are designed, built and operated," said Andrew Anagnost, president and CEO of Autodesk. "Amy and the AEC team have built a strong business and laid the foundation for the next phase of growth, with Forma becoming the industry cloud for AEC and AI helping customers navigate increasing complexity across the project lifecycle. Diana is the right leader for this moment. She brings a proven track record of leading through major technology shifts, aligning products, data and teams behind a clear vision, and turning innovation into tangible customer outcomes. Combined with her deep understanding of Autodesk and the industries we serve, Diana is uniquely positioned to build on this momentum and help shape the future of AEC."
In her new role, Colella will advance the Forma strategy while continuing to evolve our desktop products such as Revit and Civil 3D while connecting them more closely to Forma workflows. By bringing together the data and context created across the project lifecycle, Autodesk aims to make AI more useful in the work customers do every day, helping teams reduce friction, make better-informed decisions and increase their capacity to design and build.
Colella brings nearly three decades of Autodesk leadership experience spanning finance, strategy, sales, operations, product management and industry leadership. She joined Autodesk through the acquisition of Discreet Logic and has since held leadership roles across the company, including leading Autodesk's AutoCAD business and helping launch One AutoCAD. Her broad experience has given her deep insight into how Autodesk's products, operations and go-to-market teams work together to create customer success.
Most recently, Colella led the AI transformation of Autodesk's Media & Entertainment (M&E) business, where she advanced the Flow platform strategy and expanded Autodesk's role across the production lifecycle. Through acquisitions including Moxion, PIX and Wonder Dynamics, and the continued development of Autodesk Flow Studio, she helped broaden the value Autodesk delivers to creators and studios. Colella will continue to oversee the M&E business and will open a search for a new leader, reporting directly to her.
"Our customers are being asked to deliver more while navigating greater complexity, persistent resource constraints and rapid technological change," said Colella. "My priority is to listen to them, build on the strong foundation Amy and the team have created, and make sure the work we're doing across Forma and AI translates into meaningful improvements in how projects are designed, built and operated. I'm honored to lead Autodesk's AEC business at such an important moment for our customers and the industry."
The world's designers, engineers, builders, and creators trust Autodesk to help them design and make anything. From the buildings we live and work in, to the cars we drive and the bridges we drive over. From the products we use and rely on, to the movies and games that inspire us. Autodesk's Design and Make Platform unlocks the power of data to accelerate insights and automate processes, empowering customers with the technology to create the world around us and deliver better outcomes for their businesses and the planet. For more information, visit autodesk.com or follow @autodesk. #MakeAnything

Is Autodesk Still The Best Way To Own Faster Software Growth?
Thu, October 15, 2026 at 5:52 PM CDT 4 min read
Autodesk (ADSK) stock lost 24.9% over the past year, while shares of Fair Isaac (FICO) fell 56.4%. Underneath those market declines, however, business at both software companies is accelerating. Each firm has posted faster sales growth in each of the past two years, and buyers of either stock are likely betting on that continued momentum. The similarities end there. The two companies operate with completely different financial structures. Fair Isaac retains far more of its sales as profit, yet Autodesk carries substantially less debt. So which of the two does the evidence favor?
In August, Autodesk Gave A Mixed Outlook
On August 27, Autodesk adjusted its expectations for the fiscal year ending in January 2027. The company raised its revenue forecast to a midpoint of $8.32 billion, up from $8.19 billion, and also increased its billings forecast. At the same time, it lowered its reported operating margin forecast down to 26.0% at the midpoint, from 27.0%.
Fair Isaac delivered a uniformly positive update on July 29, 2026. The company raised every forecast it gave for revenue, net income and earnings per share. For the fiscal year that ended in September 2026, management guided for $2.53 billion in revenue. Final results for that period are still to come.
Those optimistic projections arrived two months before a major industry announcement.
On September 28, the Federal Housing Finance Agency said the mortgage pricing grid is being simplified and that VantageScore is being incorporated. Fair Isaac stock fell after that statement the next day.
Autodesk Keeps Less Of Each Dollar, Holds More Cash
Looking at profitability, the two businesses operate in different tiers. Autodesk turned 27.9% of its sales into operating profit over the twelve months to July 2026. By contrast, Fair Isaac converted 52.1% of its sales into operating profit over the twelve months to June 2026.
When evaluating the balance sheet, Autodesk holds a commanding advantage. As of July 31, 2026, the company held $4.16 billion in cash and short-term investments, which easily exceeded its $3.71 billion of debt. Fair Isaac sits in a much tighter position. At June 30, 2026, the company owed $5.6 billion in debt against just $248 million of cash and short-term investments.
Fair Isaac trades at a notable discount relative to its bottom line. The stock trades at 20.0 times its earnings over the past twelve months. Investors are paying a higher premium for Autodesk, which trades at 29.6 times trailing earnings.
The top line also favors Fair Isaac. The company expanded sales by 24.1% over the twelve months to June 2026, easily outpacing the 17.9% growth Autodesk recorded over the twelve months to July 2026. Expanding the timeline reveals a similar pattern. Over its last three twelve-month periods, Fair Isaac averaged 17.7% growth, compared to 14.4% for Autodesk.
Autodesk reclaims the advantage regarding debt. The company carries debt equal to 7.6% of its market value. That sits well below the 34.4% ratio for Fair Isaac.
Based on its earnings multiple, growth, margin and forecasts, Fair Isaac comes out ahead, while Autodesk owes far less. The key variable remains timing. Fair Isaac issued its results and forecasts entirely before the agency's September move. The company expects to release its first report since that development on or around November 11, 2026. You should watch what Fair Isaac says about revenue in that report.
How To Act On ADSK?

Expedia Group launches AUTONOMOUS ONBOARDING, helping properties access global travel demand faster
Tue, October 20, 2026 at 8:00 AM CDT 3 min read
Properties can join Expedia Group through their existing software and go live in under 24 hours.
The launch gives properties a simpler path to Expedia Group's consumer brands, B2B network and AI agentic bookings.
Five connectivity partners across multiple markets shaped the experience in pilot: HotelRunner, Yanolja Cloud Solutions, RoomCloud, RateGain and Eviivo.
SEATTLE, October 20, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Expedia Group today announced AUTONOMOUS ONBOARDING™, a faster, simpler way for properties to join its global travel marketplace without leaving the connectivity software they already use. With just a few clicks, properties can select Expedia Group as a distribution channel, accept their agreement and go live in less than 24 hours - without a separate onboarding workflow or duplicate data entry.
Properties select Expedia Group as a distribution channel within their existing connectivity provider, review and accept their agreement, and connect – with no separate onboarding process and no re-entering information across systems.
From there, work that once required manual setup now happens automatically. Expedia Group's technology reaches into the property's existing software and transfers the critical data needed to set up the hotel, including room types, rates and rate plans, photos, amenities, payment setups, availability, and other property details. That data is then validated by Expedia Group, so the property can go live quickly.
Once live, properties can reach travelers through Expedia Group's multiple consumer brands, its B2B distribution network of more than 75,000 partners and 200,000 travel advisors, and its emerging AI-powered travel partnerships. Expedia Group's platform saw more than one billion average monthly searches and recorded more than 415 million booked room nights in 2025, giving properties access to significant global demand1.
Ahead of the launch, Expedia Group partnered with five pilot providers to bring Autonomous Onboarding to life: HotelRunner, Yanolja Cloud Solutions, RoomCloud, RateGain and Eviivo.
"Adding a new source of demand should not add a new layer of work," said Chris Hodges, VP of Global Connectivity & Partner Solutions, Expedia Group. "Autonomous Onboarding makes it much easier for properties to join Expedia Group through the technology they already use. It is an important first step in our broader vision for AUTONOMOUS DISTRIBUTION, where partners can spend less time on manual processes and more time growing their business."
Autonomous Onboarding is the first phase of Expedia Group's Autonomous Distribution journey. Beginning with onboarding, the longer-term vision is to make the full distribution lifecycle simpler and more intelligent, extending into how partners manage and, over time, optimize their business.

Expedia Group, Inc. (EXPE) Trades Below Its Old Earnings Multiple. Is AI a Real Threat to Growth?
Mon, October 19, 2026 at 10:12 PM CDT 5 min read
Expedia Group, Inc. (NASDAQ:EXPE) is entering a new phase of the online travel debate. Artificial intelligence may become another channel through which people book rooms, or it may weaken the ability of established booking platforms to attract travelers directly. Expedia Group, Inc.'s September 23 announcement that it would work with Meta's Muse assistant puts both possibilities into focus. The company could supply bookings to a new interface, but it may also surrender part of the customer relationship to whoever controls that interface.
Expedia Group, Inc. ranks eighth among the 10 best undervalued stocks to buy now according to Reddit. Its ranking is based on hedge fund positioning, not a claim that its travel business is immune to disruption. Which of the seven stocks above it attracted stronger institutional interest, and how many face an equally direct challenge to their customer relationships?
Muse is not Expedia Group, Inc. (NASDAQ:EXPE)'s only attempt to monetize traffic it does not originate. A September 22 advertising collaboration with Redion extended the company's advertising business into travel insurance, building on a longstanding protection-services relationship. Neither announcement includes a disclosed near-term contribution to earnings, however. Their importance lies in whether Expedia Group, Inc. can earn commission or advertising revenue when trip discovery moves away from its own websites.
The operating data leave room for both interpretations. In second-quarter 2026 coverage, Expedia Group, Inc.'s gross bookings rose 12%, with business-to-business bookings expanding 21% and B2B revenue rising 23%. That partner business had delivered twenty consecutive quarters of double-digit booking growth. A booking made through a bank, airline or other partner does not depend on an Expedia consumer visiting its own app, supporting an argument that the platform can adapt to new distribution models.
However, Morgan Stanley's September 16 downgrade identified a different problem: monthly active users were flat year-over-year, compared with growth of roughly 6% at Booking.com and 10% at Airbnb, according to the bank's estimates. If customer acquisition becomes more expensive while direct traffic stagnates, incremental booking revenue may require more marketing spending. Our earlier report on Morgan Stanley's Expedia Group, Inc. downgrade examines why rising B2B bookings did not fully answer the bank's concern about consumer engagement.
The Seeking Alpha data places Expedia Group, Inc. (NASDAQ:EXPE) at 17.07 times trailing GAAP earnings and 14.76 times forward GAAP earnings. On a non-GAAP basis, the forward P/E is 13.07 times, compared with the company's five-year average of 23.84 times and the sector median of 14.84 times. Forward enterprise value to EBITDA is 7.94 times, versus 9.30 times for the sector and 8.91 times for Expedia Group, Inc.'s five-year average. The shares therefore carry a discount on several forward measures, though the relevant issue is whether the earnings behind those measures can hold up.
The same consensus projects EPS growth of 32.54% for 2026, slowing to 16.72% in 2027, 14.33% in 2028, and 3.45% in 2029. At the current share price, implied estimated earnings multiples descend from 13.07 times in 2026 to 11.20 times in 2027, and 9.79 times in 2028. That trajectory assumes Expedia Group, Inc. continues converting bookings into rising per-share profit while AI-related disruption remains manageable. It does not price a proven collapse in the intermediary model, nor does it guarantee that one will not occur.
There is a balance-sheet dimension to the discount as well. The data shows $7.13 billion of cash and $5.69 billion of debt, leaving net cash of approximately $1.44 billion before other obligations. It also places trailing price-to-cash-flow at 6.32 times against an 8.79-times sector median. Cash generation and repurchases can support per-share earnings during slower organic growth, but neither can permanently protect the multiple if the cost of winning travel bookings rises.
Wall Street Is Debating the Speed, Not Just the Direction
Wells Fargo cut its target to $275 from $307 on October 7 while maintaining Equal Weight, expecting the third quarter to mark a low point in room-night growth and describing choppy demand. Truist reduced its target to $288 from $309, keeping Hold, and warned that the AI threat was still more clearly visible in sentiment than in demonstrable profit erosion. Morgan Stanley took the firmer Underweight stance at $235, citing weaker consumer differentiation and risks from suppliers selling directly.
Those views differ in severity but meet at the same question: how much future distribution and marketing expense should be embedded in today's earnings estimates?
A useful comparison is Airbnb, whose inventory and direct traffic may be harder for AI booking agents to reproduce. Why does Airbnb's growth command a different valuation, and how does that comparison change the Expedia Group, Inc. debate? Expedia Group, Inc. (NASDAQ:EXPE)'s strength in partner distribution is real; the difficulty is deciding how much protection it provides if consumer-facing discovery migrates elsewhere.
Institutional Positioning Shows the Disagreement
Hedge fund holders declined from 62 in Q1 to 55 in Q2 2026. Meanwhile, reported short interest increased from 5.20 million shares on August 31 to 7.92 million on September 30, representing 8.50% of the float. Those observations cannot identify why individual investors traded, but they provide context for a valuation that appears undemanding relative to its history. A separate Booking-versus-Airbnb comparison illustrates how margins, proprietary supply and cash flow can reshape the online travel valuation hierarchy.
For Expedia Group, Inc. (NASDAQ:EXPE), the deciding variables are partner bookings growth, consumer user retention and whether any AI-driven bookings preserve sufficient economics to support consensus EPS.
While we acknowledge the risk and potential of EXPE as an investment, our conviction lies in the belief that some AI stocks hold greater promise for delivering higher returns and doing so within a shorter time frame. The company is adding boutique and independent hotels, Experiences, Services, sponsored advertising, smarter fees, and AI-powered search, and it says artificial intelligence has already cut the time it takes to build and launch new features by as much as 60%. Airbnb is also on solid financial footing, holding about $9.6 billion in net cash after accounting for its debt, and it generated $4.6 billion in operating cash flow in fiscal 2025.
Management expects revenue to keep growing at least in the low double digits for all of 2026, signaling confidence that this isn't just a one-quarter boost. If artificial intelligence keeps improving how well the platform converts browsers into bookings, and if hotels, Experiences, Services, and advertising start contributing more meaningfully, bulls see multiple future growth drivers rather than reliance on home rentals alone. Consensus estimates call for earnings per share of $5.30 looking ahead, about 24% higher than the $4.26 posted over the past year, which would help justify the stock's premium valuation if it plays out. That said, Airbnb has only beaten Wall Street's earnings estimates once in its last four reported quarters, missing the other three by an average of 6%, so it still has to prove it can turn growth into consistently stronger profits.
Wall Street is only moderately optimistic about the stock from here. The average analyst price target sits at $180.57, about 6% above the current share price of $169.63, while the analysts are split fairly widely: the most bullish target of $220 implies roughly 30% upside, while the most bearish target of $125 implies about 26% downside. Given that the stock already trades near 40 times trailing earnings, investors should watch closely whether Airbnb's growth, margins, and expansion into new products stay strong enough to support that price tag. The wide spread in analyst targets shows how much disagreement there is about what happens if growth slows or execution stumbles.
Regulation is a key risk to watch. Airbnb needs enough legally available listings in major tourist cities to keep growing its bookings, but rules are moving in the opposite direction. Barcelona plans to eliminate short-term rental licenses entirely by 2028, and London, Paris, and Rome have already added various caps and restrictions. A new European Union data-sharing framework could also make it easier for local governments to find and remove listings that don't comply with the rules. On top of that, a weaker job market, slower economic growth, or rising travel costs could push cautious travelers toward cheaper options and dent bookings. With regulatory pressure building and the stock still priced near 40 times trailing earnings, there isn't much room for growth to slow down without the valuation starting to look expensive.
Hedge fund positioning shows a cautious signal. As per our database, 75 hedge funds held Airbnb, Inc. at the end of the second quarter, down from 87 the quarter before. That drop suggests institutional investors grew more cautious on the stock even as its underlying growth and margins remained strong, hinting at unease about how long that growth can support its rich valuation. By comparison, Booking Holdings was held by 92 hedge funds, down from 95, Expedia Group was held by 55 hedge funds, down from 62, and Trip.com Group (NASDAQ:TCOM) was held by 28 hedge funds, down from 38. Booking Holdings held onto the most stable institutional support, Trip.com Group saw the sharpest pullback, and Airbnb, Inc.'s decline in hedge fund interest was steeper than Booking Holdings (NASDAQ:BKNG)'s despite Airbnb's stronger growth numbers.
Short interest data also paints a fairly cautious picture. About 3.50% of Airbnb, Inc.'s available shares are sold short, higher than Booking Holdings at 2.62% and Trip.com Group at 1.90%, though still lower than Expedia Group at 6.75%. This suggests investors are more skeptical of Airbnb, Inc.'s premium price tag and regulatory exposure than they are of Booking Holdings or Trip.com Group, but less skeptical than they are of Expedia Group.
ABNB's forward P/E is 25.38. Booking Holdings Inc., Expedia Group, Inc., and Trip.com Group Limited trade at forward P/Es of 13.28, 11.29, and 11.72, respectively. ABNB's own forward P/E was 27.47 at the end of 2025, so its multiple has fallen approximately 8%, but investors still pay roughly twice as much for each dollar of expected earnings as they would for its peers. We believe 25.38 times forward earnings is a demanding valuation for a stock like ABNB. This means investors who buy ABNB at this valuation are pretty much betting that faster booking growth and expansion into new categories will keep earnings growing strongly for several years. Airbnb, Inc.'s earnings per share were $4.26 over the past year, while the supplied consensus estimate is $5.30 looking ahead. This puts its expected earnings growth rate at approximately 24%. We believe ABNB's expected earnings growth could justify its premium if the company delivers on those forecasts. Its expansion into new categories offers room for further gains, but at 25.38 times forward earnings, investors are paying for continued success rather than buying an obvious bargain.
Previously, we covered a bullish thesis on Airbnb, Inc. (ABNB) by Chit Chat Stocks in May 2025, which highlighted Experiences and Services as drivers of engagement, user spending, and expansion beyond accommodations. ABNB's stock price has appreciated by approximately 19.32% since our coverage. We believe ABNB could be a good long-term investment, provided its earnings growth lives up to expectations.
Airbnb, Inc. is not on our list of the 40 Most Popular Stocks Among Hedge Funds. While ABNB may see further gains if faster booking growth and expansion into hotels, Experiences, Services, and advertising drive stronger earnings, we believe some AI stocks offer stronger long-term potential, with a high probability of delivering superior returns on a much shorter timeline. Expedia Group Automates Hotel Onboarding to Speed Marketplace Entry
Properties can now join Expedia Group’s global travel marketplace through their existing connectivity software, with a few clicks, and go live in less than 24 hours, the company said in a Tuesday (Oct. 20) press release.
This simpler path is enabled by Expedia Group’s new Autonomous Onboarding, according to the release.
With Autonomous Onboarding, properties can go to their existing connectivity software, select Expedia Group as a distribution channel, review and accept their agreement, and connect, the release said.

After that, Expedia Group’s technology reaches into the property’s connectivity software to transfer the data needed to set up the hotel, Expedia Group validates the data and the property goes live in less than 24 hours, per the release.
Once live, properties can reach travelers through Expedia Group’s consumer brands, which include Expedia, Hotels.com and Vrbo; its B2B distribution network, which includes 75,000 partners and 200,000 travel advisors; and its emerging artificial intelligence-powered travel partnerships, according to the release.
“Adding a new source of demand should not add a new layer of work,” Chris Hodges, vice president of global connectivity and partner solutions at Expedia Group, said in the release. “Autonomous Onboarding makes it much easier for properties to join Expedia Group through the technology they already use.”
PYMNTS reported in August that during Expedia Group’s second quarter earnings call, executives argued that the company’s strategy of pairing artificial intelligence investments with a fast-growing B2B business is giving it multiple engines for growth.
Expedia Group said in a June press release that it was embarking on a journey to reduce friction in the day-to-day operations of hotels. The company said this initiative, dubbed “Autonomous Distribution,” would be implemented in three phases. The phases include Autonomous Onboarding, Autonomous Management that will use software to streamline day-to-day operations and Autonomous Optimization that will provide promotional levers and expanded distribution to improve hotels’ performance.
In the Tuesday press release, Hodges said that the newly launched Autonomous Onboarding “is an important first step in our broader vision for Autonomous Distribution, where partners can spend less time on manual processes and more time growing their businesses.

Expedia Group Launches AUTONOMOUS ONBOARDING, Helping Properties Access Global Travel Demand Faster
Expedia Group launches AUTONOMOUS ONBOARDING, helping properties access global travel demand faster
Tue, October 20, 2026 at 8:00 AM CDT 3 min read
Properties can join Expedia Group through their existing software and go live in under 24 hours.
The launch gives properties a simpler path to Expedia Group's consumer brands, B2B network and AI agentic bookings.
Five connectivity partners across multiple markets shaped the experience in pilot: HotelRunner, Yanolja Cloud Solutions, RoomCloud, RateGain and Eviivo.
SEATTLE, October 20, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Expedia Group today announced AUTONOMOUS ONBOARDING™, a faster, simpler way for properties to join its global travel marketplace without leaving the connectivity software they already use. With just a few clicks, properties can select Expedia Group as a distribution channel, accept their agreement and go live in less than 24 hours - without a separate onboarding workflow or duplicate data entry.
Properties select Expedia Group as a distribution channel within their existing connectivity provider, review and accept their agreement, and connect – with no separate onboarding process and no re-entering information across systems.
From there, work that once required manual setup now happens automatically. Expedia Group's technology reaches into the property's existing software and transfers the critical data needed to set up the hotel, including room types, rates and rate plans, photos, amenities, payment setups, availability, and other property details. That data is then validated by Expedia Group, so the property can go live quickly.
Once live, properties can reach travelers through Expedia Group's multiple consumer brands, its B2B distribution network of more than 75,000 partners and 200,000 travel advisors, and its emerging AI-powered travel partnerships. Expedia Group's platform saw more than one billion average monthly searches and recorded more than 415 million booked room nights in 2025, giving properties access to significant global demand1.
Ahead of the launch, Expedia Group partnered with five pilot providers to bring Autonomous Onboarding to life: HotelRunner, Yanolja Cloud Solutions, RoomCloud, RateGain and Eviivo.
"Adding a new source of demand should not add a new layer of work," said Chris Hodges, VP of Global Connectivity & Partner Solutions, Expedia Group. "Autonomous Onboarding makes it much easier for properties to join Expedia Group through the technology they already use. It is an important first step in our broader vision for AUTONOMOUS DISTRIBUTION, where partners can spend less time on manual processes and more time growing their business."
Autonomous Onboarding is the first phase of Expedia Group's Autonomous Distribution journey. Beginning with onboarding, the longer-term vision is to make the full distribution lifecycle simpler and more intelligent, extending into how partners manage and, over time, optimize their business.
Learn more about Autonomous Onboarding at: Expedia Group Connectivity.

Expedia Group, Inc. (EXPE) Trades Below Its Old Earnings Multiple. Is AI a Real Threat to Growth?
Mon, October 19, 2026 at 10:12 PM CDT 5 min read
Expedia Group, Inc. (NASDAQ:EXPE) is entering a new phase of the online travel debate. Artificial intelligence may become another channel through which people book rooms, or it may weaken the ability of established booking platforms to attract travelers directly. Expedia Group, Inc.'s September 23 announcement that it would work with Meta's Muse assistant puts both possibilities into focus. The company could supply bookings to a new interface, but it may also surrender part of the customer relationship to whoever controls that interface.
Expedia Group, Inc. ranks eighth among the 10 best undervalued stocks to buy now according to Reddit. Its ranking is based on hedge fund positioning, not a claim that its travel business is immune to disruption. Which of the seven stocks above it attracted stronger institutional interest, and how many face an equally direct challenge to their customer relationships?
Muse is not Expedia Group, Inc. (NASDAQ:EXPE)'s only attempt to monetize traffic it does not originate. A September 22 advertising collaboration with Redion extended the company's advertising business into travel insurance, building on a longstanding protection-services relationship. Neither announcement includes a disclosed near-term contribution to earnings, however. Their importance lies in whether Expedia Group, Inc. can earn commission or advertising revenue when trip discovery moves away from its own websites.
The operating data leave room for both interpretations. In second-quarter 2026 coverage, Expedia Group, Inc.'s gross bookings rose 12%, with business-to-business bookings expanding 21% and B2B revenue rising 23%. That partner business had delivered twenty consecutive quarters of double-digit booking growth. A booking made through a bank, airline or other partner does not depend on an Expedia consumer visiting its own app, supporting an argument that the platform can adapt to new distribution models.
However, Morgan Stanley's September 16 downgrade identified a different problem: monthly active users were flat year-over-year, compared with growth of roughly 6% at Booking.com and 10% at Airbnb, according to the bank's estimates. If customer acquisition becomes more expensive while direct traffic stagnates, incremental booking revenue may require more marketing spending. Our earlier report on Morgan Stanley's Expedia Group, Inc. downgrade examines why rising B2B bookings did not fully answer the bank's concern about consumer engagement.
The Seeking Alpha data places Expedia Group, Inc. (NASDAQ:EXPE) at 17.07 times trailing GAAP earnings and 14.76 times forward GAAP earnings. On a non-GAAP basis, the forward P/E is 13.07 times, compared with the company's five-year average of 23.84 times and the sector median of 14.84 times. Forward enterprise value to EBITDA is 7.94 times, versus 9.30 times for the sector and 8.91 times for Expedia Group, Inc.'s five-year average. The shares therefore carry a discount on several forward measures, though the relevant issue is whether the earnings behind those measures can hold up.
The same consensus projects EPS growth of 32.54% for 2026, slowing to 16.72% in 2027, 14.33% in 2028, and 3.45% in 2029. At the current share price, implied estimated earnings multiples descend from 13.07 times in 2026 to 11.20 times in 2027, and 9.79 times in 2028. That trajectory assumes Expedia Group, Inc. continues converting bookings into rising per-share profit while AI-related disruption remains manageable. It does not price a proven collapse in the intermediary model, nor does it guarantee that one will not occur.
There is a balance-sheet dimension to the discount as well. The data shows $7.13 billion of cash and $5.69 billion of debt, leaving net cash of approximately $1.44 billion before other obligations. It also places trailing price-to-cash-flow at 6.32 times against an 8.79-times sector median. Cash generation and repurchases can support per-share earnings during slower organic growth, but neither can permanently protect the multiple if the cost of winning travel bookings rises.
Wall Street Is Debating the Speed, Not Just the Direction
Wells Fargo cut its target to $275 from $307 on October 7 while maintaining Equal Weight, expecting the third quarter to mark a low point in room-night growth and describing choppy demand. Truist reduced its target to $288 from $309, keeping Hold, and warned that the AI threat was still more clearly visible in sentiment than in demonstrable profit erosion. Morgan Stanley took the firmer Underweight stance at $235, citing weaker consumer differentiation and risks from suppliers selling directly.
Those views differ in severity but meet at the same question: how much future distribution and marketing expense should be embedded in today's earnings estimates?
A useful comparison is Airbnb, whose inventory and direct traffic may be harder for AI booking agents to reproduce. Why does Airbnb's growth command a different valuation, and how does that comparison change the Expedia Group, Inc. debate? Expedia Group, Inc. (NASDAQ:EXPE)'s strength in partner distribution is real; the difficulty is deciding how much protection it provides if consumer-facing discovery migrates elsewhere.
Institutional Positioning Shows the Disagreement
Hedge fund holders declined from 62 in Q1 to 55 in Q2 2026. Meanwhile, reported short interest increased from 5.20 million shares on August 31 to 7.92 million on September 30, representing 8.50% of the float. Those observations cannot identify why individual investors traded, but they provide context for a valuation that appears undemanding relative to its history. A separate Booking-versus-Airbnb comparison illustrates how margins, proprietary supply and cash flow can reshape the online travel valuation hierarchy.
For Expedia Group, Inc. (NASDAQ:EXPE), the deciding variables are partner bookings growth, consumer user retention and whether any AI-driven bookings preserve sufficient economics to support consensus EPS.
While we acknowledge the risk and potential of EXPE as an investment, our conviction lies in the belief that some AI stocks hold greater promise for delivering higher returns and doing so within a shorter time frame. If you are looking for an AI stock that is more promising than EXPE and that has 10,000% upside potential, check out our report about this cheapest AI stock.

Expedia's 15% commission is to blame for jump in hotel prices since 2020, class-action lawsuit alleges
Thu, October 15, 2026 at 10:00 AM CDT 4 min read
There are plenty of reasons the travel industry is struggling these days. Inflation has made some people rethink their plans. Trade wars and immigration policies have discouraged many international tourists from visiting the U.S., but one other big factor is the price of hotel rooms.
Since 2020, the average daily hotel rate has jumped from $103 to $162, a 58% rise over five years. And a new class-action suit, filed in the Western District of Washington, says the travel site Expedia is to blame.

The suit alleges the company "has abused its monopoly power to impose exclusionary contracts and pricing algorithms on hotels in violation of the federal antitrust laws." That, it says, has resulted in consumers having to pay "artificially inflated prices" for hotel rooms across the U.S.
In addition, the complaint alleges, consumers pay higher rates regardless of whether they use Expedia's online site or the hotel's official website.
Expedia, in a statement to Moneywise, denied all these allegations.
"The allegations in the lawsuit are meritless," a spokesperson said. "For over 30 years, Expedia has brought transparency to shopping for travel, allowing travelers to see different travel options, make informed travel decisions, and get competitive offerings and better value from travel suppliers."
Expedia's commissions are at the heart of the problem, says the suit. The site charges hotels a 15% commission on bookings made through one of its online portals. That, argue the plaintiffs, has resulted in hotels charging travelers as much as 30% more to recoup any lost profits.
Expedia is the flagship site of Expedia Group, a conglomerate that controls several of the biggest online travel portals, including Hotels.com, Vrbo, Travelocity, Hotwire, Orbitz, and Trivago. The lawsuit alleges 80% of all U.S-based online bookings happen on one of the company's sites.
"Expedia's anticompetitive Scheme has injured virtually every consumer who has booked a U.S. hotel room — whether through Expedia or not," the suit reads.
The plaintiffs are proposing two different classes to the court: People who booked a hotel room directly with the facility and another for people who booked online. The suit is seeking both financial penalties and a permanent injunction that would prevent the travel site from re-imposing its allegedly exclusionary contracts and pricing algorithms.

Hotels are just a part of the travel equation for tourists. And they're not the only field seeing big price increases.
Airfares have increased 22.4% over the past year, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics. And, for people who prefer to drive to their destination, the average price of gas has jumped roughly 40% in the past year, says AAA.
Despite the higher prices, 71% of the people surveyed by PwC in May said they planned to spend the same or more on summer travel as they did the year prior. The average spend per consumer worked out to $2,892.
