UNPACK ’27: EXPEDIA AND STAYZ REVEAL THE TRAVEL TRENDS INSPIRING THE WORLD IN 2027
Wed, October 14, 2026 at 8:01 AM CDT 7 min read
New Expedia Group report identifies five travel trends set to shape 2027, from carefree getaways and hobby-led trips to emerging destinations and the new Set-Jetting forecast.
SYDNEY, October 14, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Expedia Group today unveiled Unpack '27: The Trends in Travel™, the annual report exploring the destinations, experiences, and behaviours expected to shape travel in 2027.
Drawing on first-party insight from Expedia, and Stayz, as well as global traveller research and social listening, Unpack '27 reveals the new places drawing travellers in 2027 and some surprising things they're doing when they get there.
"Travel is about creating memories and Unpack '27 uncovers the destinations and experiences shaping those moments," said Ariane Gorin, CEO of Expedia Group. "In 2027, travellers are being more intentional in choosing their next adventure, seeking experiences that are more personal and purposeful to them. We're making it easier to discover, plan, and book the right trip, so travellers can spend less time managing the details and more time enjoying the moments that matter."
2027 Destinations of the Year — Expedia's Destinations of the Year showcases some of 2027's fastest-growing travel destinations, using real search data to track where traveller interest is climbing:
The Tweed, New South Wales, Australia ✓ (+35%)
Checkmarks designate locations recognised by Expedia's Smart Travel Health Check framework for managing tourism responsibly without overcrowding. Learn more about the Destinations of the Year and Expedia's Smart Travel Health Check here.
Un-Adulting — Travellers are reclaiming child-like joy with getaways built around play, spontaneity, and zero obligations. With Expedia data showing 50% of Aussie travellers are likely to book an Un-Adulting trip in 2027,5 theme park events just for grown-ups, immersive attractions, and nostalgic experiences are becoming the ingredients for a genuine break from being an adult. Un-Adulting trips are about wanting a carefree day (67%), a genuine break from responsibilities (56%), and want to relive childhood memories (40%).5
Among the Un-Adulting experiences to try in 2027 are Tokyo Disneyland, Tokyo, Japan; Colour Factory Chicago, Chicago, U.S.; Park Xcaret, Cancun, Mexico; and Gold Coast: Dreamworld. See the full list of Un-Adulting experiences here.
Set-Jetting — Five years after Expedia Group first named Set-Jetting as a travel trend, screen-inspired travel continues to turn fictional worlds and filming locations into real-world itineraries. Nearly 1 in 5 travellers now report having booked a trip to a destination after seeing it featured in a TV show or movie.5
Nearly half of the travellers surveyed reported proactively researching or booking trips to destinations from upcoming TV shows and movies that haven't even been released yet, rising to 57% among Gen Z and Millennials.5 On social media, mentions of traveling to Miami increased by 64% year-over-year driven by the upcoming Miami Vice reboot.4
More than 25 years on, The Lord of the Rings remains the world's No.1 top set-jetting driver (27%), and with The Lord of the Rings: The Hunt for Gollum set to hit screens next year, New Zealand is primed for a fresh wave of set-jetting demand. 7
Other titles on the 2027 forecast include Emily in Paris Season 6, The White Lotus Season 4, Heated Rivalry Season 2, Miami Vice '85, K-Pop: The Debut, Beach Read, Day Drinker, and the Ocean's Eleven prequel. These anticipated releases are putting destinations on travellers' maps before the first episode or scene arrives. Learn more about Set-Jetting here.
Hobby Hubs — For a growing number of travellers, trip planning starts with a passion rather than a destination, with Stayz research showing 88% are likely to take a hobby-focused trip in 2027.6 Holiday rentals are becoming gathering places for crafting weekends, photography retreats, board-game nights, birding trips, and antiquing escapes with 31% of Aussie travellers saying hobbies play a bigger role in how they travel compared to five years ago.6
Connection is key for those looking to engage in hobby holidays. The leading motivations for booking a Hobby Hub are spending time with people who share similar interests (51%), enjoying a hobby in a new setting (46%) and spending time on a hobby (37%).6 Hobby Hubs bring people together around the activities they love, creating space to connect and enjoy those passions in a new setting.
Some great holiday rentals for Hobby trips include The Hiker's House, Jarrahdale, Western Australia, Australia, and The Play House, Winchelsea South, Victoria, Australia. See more on Hobby Hubs here.
Heartland Holidays — Beach getaways may be the first destinations that come to mind when considering holiday home rentals, but Stayz has seen dramatic growth in interest for inland destinations. Searches rose most sharply for Canberra, ACT (+55%); Crackenback, NSW (+45%), and Mount Hotham, VIC (+40%), with Nannup, WA and Blue Mountains, NSW also gaining ground.3 These smaller towns, and mountain escapes offer local character, cultural energy, outdoor access, and a slower pace away from the usual coastal hotspots.
Nearly 57% of travellers have gone on holiday to non-coastal destinations in the past 12 months, with the top driver for visiting landlocked locales being interest in the local culture, food, and art scenes, followed by a desire to explore off-the-beaten-path places, and affordability.6
To learn more about Unpack '27: The Trends in Travel™, visit www.expedia.com.au/newsroom for the full report, downloadable assets, and brand-specific insights from Expedia and Stayz.
1. Destinations of the Year: Based on increases in flight and accommodation searches on Expedia from 1 September, 2025, to 27 July, 2026, vs. 1 September 1, 2024, to 27 July, 2025.
A checkmark denotes destinations that meet the Smart Travel Health Check framework, aligned with World Travel & Tourism Council (WTTC) principles. The Smart Travel Health Check helps travellers identify destinations that offer rich cultural and natural experiences without the overcrowding seen in many of the world's most popular cities.
2. Un-Adulting: Social media data based on mentions of "Un-Adulting," "carefree travel," and similar terms on X, Reddit, Instagram, TikTok, and Facebook from 15 April to 30 June, 2026, versus the same period in 2025.
3. Heartland Holidays: Based on holiday rental searches on Stayz.com.au from 1 September, 2025, to 31 May, 2026, versus 1 September, 2024, to 30 April, 2025.
4. Set-Jetting: Search data based on accommodation, flight, and/or package searches on Expedia Group brands in the 30 days after relevant title or filming announcements versus the prior 30 days.
Social media data based on mentions of the shows/films along with travel terms on online news outlets, blogs, and social channels including X, Reddit, Instagram, TikTok, and Facebook from 1 March, 2026, to 10 June, 2026, compared to the same period the previous year.

The study was conducted online between 4 August, 2026, and 14 August, 2026, among 2,000 adult respondents across Australia, who are planning domestic or international travel in the next three years.
6. Third-party research was conducted by market research company OnePoll in accordance with the Market Research Society's code of conduct. The study was conducted online between August 4, 2026, and 18 August, 2026, among 1,000 adults across Australia who have stayed in a holiday rental.

Expedia Signs as Official Travel Partner of the NHL in the U.S. and Canada
SEATTLE & NEW YORK, October 13, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Expedia® and the National Hockey League (NHL®) today announced a multi-year North American partnership naming Expedia the Official Travel Partner of the NHL in North America. As part of the agreement, Expedia will gain marketing rights and NHL designations in the U.S. and Canada. In addition to maintaining its exclusive status as the Official Travel Partner of the NHL in North America, Expedia also retains exclusive rights in Online Travel, Vacation Rentals, and Hotels.
Through the partnership, Expedia will have brand presence on the NHL's digitally enhanced dasherboards throughout the regular season and Stanley Cup Playoffs. Expedia will also be part of some of the League's most iconic events, including NHL All-Star Weekend, NHL Heritage Classic™, NHL Winter Classic®, and NHL Stadium Series™.
The partnership extends online as well, where Expedia will serve as the presenting sponsor of the Stanley Cup® Playoffs Bracket Challenge and the Stanley Cup Playoffs Second Chance Bracket. NHL.com will also provide NHL fans with a website linked opportunity to combine travel with regular season or Stanley Cup Playoffs games. Together, the activations and digital touch points are designed to give traveling fans an easy way to engage in the NHL season and allow them to plan their next trip around games.
"NHL fans will go near and far to support their team," said Tracey Weber, General Manager, Expedia. "We're excited to partner with the NHL to help fans easily plan and book trips to cheer on their favorite team, whether it's traveling for a regular season game or flying across the country for the Stanley Cup Playoffs. From take off to puck drop, Expedia can help fans get there, stay there and make the most of every NHL travel experience, while saving when they bundle flights, hotels and more."
"We're thrilled to welcome Expedia as our Official Travel Partner, at such an exciting time for the League," said George Dudas, NHL Vice President, Business Development. "Our fans are at the center of everything we do, and this partnership gives our fans new ways to combine travel and memorable NHL moments — from the start of the season through the Stanley Cup Playoffs."
Expedia and the NHL will continue to share details on fan experiences planned for the League's marquee events, along with travel-focused content for fans to make the most of the NHL season.

Airbnb (ABNB) vs. EXPE and TCOM: Can Double-Digit Growth Offset Rising Regulatory Pressure?
Wed, October 14, 2026 at 11:45 AM CDT 7 min read
Is ABNB a good stock to buy? We came across a bullish thesis on Airbnb, Inc. on Astute Optics - US's Substack. In this article, we will summarize the bulls' thesis on ABNB. Airbnb, Inc.'s share was trading at $163.23 as of October 8th 2026. ABNB's trailing and forward P/E were 34.15 and 25.38 respectively according to Yahoo Finance.
This isn't the first time we see a vacation rental platform pitched as a great investment. ABNB shares gained 33.69% over the last 12 months. Comparable stocks like Expedia Group (EXPE) gained 19.39% during the same period. Why are travel stocks rising so much and is it really a good time to buy them?
Airbnb, Inc. (ABNB)'s Chesky says App can become an ‘Amazon for services’
In July, we published an article about the 8 Best Stocks to Buy Following Federal Reserve Pivot Expectations and ABNB ranked #4 in that article. ABNB returned 11.54% since then. So, hedge funds were right about ABNB. This article explains why hedge funds were bullish on ABNB. Before getting into our analysis, let's take a look at the business and why some investors like the stock so much.
Airbnb, Inc. (NASDAQ:ABNB) operates a global online marketplace connecting hosts and guests for stays, experiences, and services. The big question for investors is whether Airbnb can keep growing beyond home rentals into hotels, Experiences, Services, advertising, and AI-powered travel tools, even as regulators tighten the rules around short-term rentals. Airbnb's business model requires little capital, runs on healthy margins, and its bookings are growing faster than major rivals in online travel.
Read More: 15 AI Stocks That Are Quietly Making Investors Rich
Read More: Undervalued AI Stock Poised For Massive Gains: 10000% Upside Potential
In the second quarter of fiscal 2026, revenue rose 17% year over year to about $3.6 billion, and the number of nights and experiences booked grew 10%, outpacing 6% growth at Expedia Group (NASDAQ:EXPE) and 5% at Booking Holdings (NASDAQ:BKNG). Over the past twelve months, revenue grew 13.6% to roughly $13.2 billion. Even so, the stock trades at about 39.8 times trailing earnings, well above the peer median of roughly 26.7 times, meaning investors are already paying up for several more years of strong growth to materialize. You can check out whether Booking or Airbnb is the better stock to buy here.
The bullish case is built on Airbnb continuing to outgrow the broader travel market by using its large base of travelers and hosts to expand into new categories. The company is adding boutique and independent hotels, Experiences, Services, sponsored advertising, smarter fees, and AI-powered search, and it says artificial intelligence has already cut the time it takes to build and launch new features by as much as 60%. Airbnb is also on solid financial footing, holding about $9.6 billion in net cash after accounting for its debt, and it generated $4.6 billion in operating cash flow in fiscal 2025.
Management expects revenue to keep growing at least in the low double digits for all of 2026, signaling confidence that this isn't just a one-quarter boost. If artificial intelligence keeps improving how well the platform converts browsers into bookings, and if hotels, Experiences, Services, and advertising start contributing more meaningfully, bulls see multiple future growth drivers rather than reliance on home rentals alone. Consensus estimates call for earnings per share of $5.30 looking ahead, about 24% higher than the $4.26 posted over the past year, which would help justify the stock's premium valuation if it plays out. That said, Airbnb has only beaten Wall Street's earnings estimates once in its last four reported quarters, missing the other three by an average of 6%, so it still has to prove it can turn growth into consistently stronger profits.
Wall Street is only moderately optimistic about the stock from here. The average analyst price target sits at $180.57, about 6% above the current share price of $169.63, while the analysts are split fairly widely: the most bullish target of $220 implies roughly 30% upside, while the most bearish target of $125 implies about 26% downside. Given that the stock already trades near 40 times trailing earnings, investors should watch closely whether Airbnb's growth, margins, and expansion into new products stay strong enough to support that price tag. The wide spread in analyst targets shows how much disagreement there is about what happens if growth slows or execution stumbles.
Regulation is a key risk to watch. Airbnb needs enough legally available listings in major tourist cities to keep growing its bookings, but rules are moving in the opposite direction. Barcelona plans to eliminate short-term rental licenses entirely by 2028, and London, Paris, and Rome have already added various caps and restrictions. A new European Union data-sharing framework could also make it easier for local governments to find and remove listings that don't comply with the rules. On top of that, a weaker job market, slower economic growth, or rising travel costs could push cautious travelers toward cheaper options and dent bookings. With regulatory pressure building and the stock still priced near 40 times trailing earnings, there isn't much room for growth to slow down without the valuation starting to look expensive.
Hedge fund positioning shows a cautious signal. As per our database, 75 hedge funds held Airbnb, Inc. at the end of the second quarter, down from 87 the quarter before. That drop suggests institutional investors grew more cautious on the stock even as its underlying growth and margins remained strong, hinting at unease about how long that growth can support its rich valuation. By comparison, Booking Holdings was held by 92 hedge funds, down from 95, Expedia Group was held by 55 hedge funds, down from 62, and Trip.com Group (NASDAQ:TCOM) was held by 28 hedge funds, down from 38. Booking Holdings held onto the most stable institutional support, Trip.com Group saw the sharpest pullback, and Airbnb, Inc.'s decline in hedge fund interest was steeper than Booking Holdings (NASDAQ:BKNG)'s despite Airbnb's stronger growth numbers.
Short interest data also paints a fairly cautious picture. About 3.50% of Airbnb, Inc.'s available shares are sold short, higher than Booking Holdings at 2.62% and Trip.com Group at 1.90%, though still lower than Expedia Group at 6.75%. This suggests investors are more skeptical of Airbnb, Inc.'s premium price tag and regulatory exposure than they are of Booking Holdings or Trip.com Group, but less skeptical than they are of Expedia Group.
ABNB's forward P/E is 25.38. Booking Holdings Inc., Expedia Group, Inc., and Trip.com Group Limited trade at forward P/Es of 13.28, 11.29, and 11.72, respectively. ABNB's own forward P/E was 27.47 at the end of 2025, so its multiple has fallen approximately 8%, but investors still pay roughly twice as much for each dollar of expected earnings as they would for its peers. We believe 25.38 times forward earnings is a demanding valuation for a stock like ABNB. This means investors who buy ABNB at this valuation are pretty much betting that faster booking growth and expansion into new categories will keep earnings growing strongly for several years. Airbnb, Inc.'s earnings per share were $4.26 over the past year, while the supplied consensus estimate is $5.30 looking ahead. This puts its expected earnings growth rate at approximately 24%. We believe ABNB's expected earnings growth could justify its premium if the company delivers on those forecasts. Its expansion into new categories offers room for further gains, but at 25.38 times forward earnings, investors are paying for continued success rather than buying an obvious bargain.
Previously, we covered a bullish thesis on Airbnb, Inc. (ABNB) by Chit Chat Stocks in May 2025, which highlighted Experiences and Services as drivers of engagement, user spending, and expansion beyond accommodations. ABNB's stock price has appreciated by approximately 19.32% since our coverage. We believe ABNB could be a good long-term investment, provided its earnings growth lives up to expectations.
Airbnb, Inc. is not on our list of the 40 Most Popular Stocks Among Hedge Funds. While ABNB may see further gains if faster booking growth and expansion into hotels, Experiences, Services, and advertising drive stronger earnings, we believe some AI stocks offer stronger long-term potential, with a high probability of delivering superior returns on a much shorter timeline. If you are looking for an AI stock that is more promising than ABNB and that has 10,000% upside potential, check out our report about this cheapest AI stock.
